definition_zh: 讲座；授课；（大学的）课时；讲稿；训斥
definition_en: a formal talk given to teach or inform, a course session built on such talks, the written text of a talk, a serious scolding, or, in older use, the act of reading
core_image: 讲台前的一束光：把文字拣出来，念给台下的人听
scene: 大学阶梯教室里，教授把讲义摊在讲台上。He began a lecture on the history of the city, and the students below wrote so fast that their pens never stopped.
sceneCN: 这里 lecture 是「讲座、课堂讲授」（第 2 个义项：面向听众的正式讲授）；句意：他开始一场关于城市史的讲座，下面学生的笔一直没停。图中可辨识物件：阶梯教室、讲台、摊开的讲义、投影幕、学生的笔记本。

pos.zh: 讲座；授课；（大学的）课时；讲稿；训斥
讲授；作讲座；长篇训斥

derivatives.zh: 讲座；讲授（名词与动词同形，零派生）

senses.title: Reading aloud: the act of reading
senses.titleCN: 诵读：把文字读出声
senses.definition: the act of reading a text, especially aloud and in a formal setting (now archaic)
senses.definitionCN: 阅读文本的行为，尤指在正式场合朗读（现已古旧）
senses.example: In the monastery the lecture of the psalm began at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 修道院里，晨祷时对圣咏的诵读从黎明开始。
senses.why: Lecture came from Medieval Latin lectura, 'a reading'. Before it named a talk, it named the act of reading itself, and the oldest English examples keep that plain sense.
senses.whyCN: lecture 来自中世纪拉丁语 lectura“阅读”。在它指“讲座”之前，它指的就是“读”这个行为，最早的英语用例保留着这层朴素含义。

senses.title: A formal talk that teaches
senses.titleCN: 讲座：面向听众的正式讲授
senses.definition: a formal talk given to a group of people, especially students, in order to teach or inform them
senses.definitionCN: 为教授或告知一群人（尤指学生）而作的正式讲话
senses.example: She went to a lecture on the history of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 她去听了一场关于这座城市历史的讲座。
senses.why: In the 16c a lecture was a discourse read or delivered before an audience. The act of reading aloud turned into the public teaching talk, which is now the central sense.
senses.whyCN: 在 16 世纪，lecture 指向听众读出或讲出的一段论述。“朗读”这个动作由此变成公开的教学讲话，也就是今天最核心的义项。

senses.title: A course unit: one class in a series
senses.titleCN: 课时：课程中的一个讲授单元
senses.definition: a single period of instruction in a course, or the course seen as a series of such talks
senses.definitionCN: 课程中的一节讲授，或由一系列讲授构成的整门课
senses.example: The course consists of twelve lectures and four seminars.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课由十二次讲授和四次研讨课组成。
senses.why: Once a lecture is put on a timetable, the talk becomes the unit of a course. Attendance is counted in lectures, and the syllabus is divided into them.
senses.whyCN: 一旦讲座被排进课表，这场讲话就成了课程的计量单位。出勤按“讲”计算，教学大纲也按讲次划分。

senses.title: The written text of a talk
senses.titleCN: 讲稿：写在纸上的那份讲授
senses.definition: the written text or full notes from which a talk is delivered, or a published version of it
senses.definitionCN: 演讲所依据的书面文本或完整讲稿，也指其出版形式
senses.example: She wrote out the lecture in full before rehearsing it.
senses.exampleCN: 她先把讲稿完整写出来，再开始排练。
senses.why: A talk can be fixed on paper before or after it is spoken. The same noun then names the script the speaker holds, which is why one can write, revise or print a lecture.
senses.whyCN: 讲话在说之前或之后都可以固定在纸上。同一个名词于是也指讲者手里的稿子，所以说“写讲稿、改讲稿、印讲稿”都成立。

senses.title: A serious scolding
senses.titleCN: 训斥：长篇的批评
senses.definition: a long, serious talk to someone about their behaviour, given as a warning or punishment
senses.definitionCN: 就某人的行为作长时间严肃谈话，作为警告或惩罚
senses.example: His father gave him a lecture about wasting money.
senses.exampleCN: 父亲就乱花钱的事训了他一顿。
senses.why: The instructive frame is now aimed at correction. The content is still teaching, but the listener is being told off, so praise and warning replace neutral explanation.
senses.whyCN: 讲授的框架这时对准了“纠正”：内容仍是在教，但听者是在挨批评，于是中性的讲解换成了告诫与责难。

senses.title: Verb: teach by giving talks
senses.titleCN: 动词：讲授、开讲座
senses.definition: to give a formal talk to students or to an audience
senses.definitionCN: 给学生或听众作正式讲授
senses.example: Professor Lin lectures on constitutional history.
senses.exampleCN: 林教授讲授宪政史。
senses.why: This is zero derivation: the noun became a verb with no added suffix, naming the activity of the person behind the lectern.
senses.whyCN: 这是零派生：名词不加任何后缀直接变成动词，指讲台后面那个人所做的事。

senses.title: Verb: scold at length
senses.titleCN: 动词：长篇训斥
senses.definition: to talk seriously and at length to someone about something they have done wrong
senses.definitionCN: 就某人做错的事进行长时间严肃谈话
senses.example: The coach lectured the team for giving up in the second half.
senses.exampleCN: 教练因球队下半场放弃而训了他们一顿。
senses.why: The verb takes the corrective branch too. Now it has a target and a fault, and the length of the talk is part of the reproach.
senses.whyCN: 动词也接上了“纠正”这一支：此时它带有对象和过错，而“讲得很长”本身就是责难的一部分。

senses.title: A public lecture as an event
senses.titleCN: 公开讲座：作为活动的讲演
senses.definition: a public talk organized as an event, often by a university, museum or learned society
senses.definitionCN: 作为活动组织的公开演讲，常由大学、博物馆或学术团体举办
senses.example: The museum's annual lecture drew an audience of five hundred.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆的年度讲座吸引了五百名听众。
senses.why: The form spreads beyond the classroom. A lecture can now be an event with a title, a guest speaker and tickets, even when no course is involved.
senses.whyCN: 这种形式走出了课堂。lecture 现在可以是一场有标题、有嘉宾讲者、需要门票的活动，即使并不附属于任何课程。

intro.en: Lecture is a reading word before it is a teaching word. Latin legere 'to read' goes back to 'pick out, gather', and English first used lecture for the act of reading, then for the talk.
intro.cn: lecture 先是“阅读”词，后来才是“教学”词。拉丁语 legere“读”的本义是“拣出、采集”；英语先用它指阅读行为，再指讲授。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'the act of reading, a reading aloud', borrowed from Medieval Latin lectura.
items.cn: 最早记录于 14 世纪晚期的英语，意为“阅读行为、朗读”，借自中世纪拉丁语 lectura。

items.en: lectura 'a reading' is a noun of action from lectus, the past participle of legere 'to read'.
items.cn: lectura“阅读”是由 legere“读”的过去分词 lectus 构成的行为名词。

items.en: legere meant 'to read', but its older sense was 'to pick out, select, gather'. Reading is pictured as picking out letters one by one from the page.
items.cn: legere 意为“读”，更早的意思是“拣出、挑选、采集”。阅读被想象成从页面上把字母一个个拣出来。

items.en: legere is traced to PIE *leg- 'to collect, gather, pick out'. The step from 'gather' to 'read' is inferred rather than attested, so this deeper link is generally accepted.
items.cn: legere 被追溯到原始印欧语 *leg-“收集、采集、拣出”。从“采集”到“读”这一步是推论而非有据可查，因此这层更深的联系属于一般认为是。

items.en: The sense 'a discourse read or delivered before an audience' appears in the 16c. By the 17c lecture is the ordinary word for a university talk, and the old 'reading' sense fades.
items.cn: “向听众读出或讲出的一段论述”这一义项见于 16 世纪。到 17 世纪，lecture 已是大学讲课的常用词，旧的“阅读”义逐渐退场。

items.en: Lecture and legal are not the same family: legere is the verb 'to read', while lex (genitive legis) is the noun 'law'. Both contain the leg- shape and are traced to *leg- 'gather', but law is not a form of 'read'.
items.cn: lecture 与 legal 并非同一家族：legere 是动词“读”，lex（属格 legis）是名词“法”。两者都含 leg- 这一形，都被追溯到 *leg-“采集”，但“法”并不是“读”的某种形式。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the reading root legere from the law noun lex. The near-meaning group separates a teaching talk from other kinds of public speech.
note.cn: 形近组把“读”的词根 legere 与“法”的名词 lex 分开；近义组把教学性讲授与其他类型的公开讲话分开。

entries.definition: a stand for a book or notes, used by someone who is reading or speaking. It comes from the same legere 'read' family, not from lecture itself.
entries.definitionCN: 供朗读或演讲者放置书本、讲稿的架子。它出自同一个 legere“读”的词族，而不是由 lecture 派生。

entries.definition: clear enough to be read. It is legere plus -ibilis 'able to be', so it describes writing that can be read, not a talk that is given.
entries.definitionCN: 字迹清楚、可辨认的。它是 legere 加 -ibilis“能够被……”，形容文字可读，而不是形容所作的讲座。

entries.definition: the body that makes laws. It looks as if it contains lecture's root, but it is lex 'law' plus lator 'proposer', so the meaning is law-making, not reading.
entries.definitionCN: 立法机关。它看起来含有 lecture 的词根，其实是 lex“法”加 lator“提出者”，所以意思是立法，而不是阅读。

entries.definition: a formal address to an audience. It is broader than lecture and need not teach anything; a lecture is expected to inform.
entries.definitionCN: 面向听众的正式讲话。它比 lecture 宽泛，不必包含教学；而 lecture 默认要传递知识。

entries.definition: a class in which a small group discusses a topic. It is interactive and smaller, while a lecture is one voice addressing many.
entries.definitionCN: 小组讨论某个主题的课程。它强调互动且人数少，而 lecture 是一个声音对许多人讲。

entries.definition: a talk on a religious or moral theme, usually delivered in worship. It aims at the conscience, not at course content.
entries.definitionCN: 关于宗教或道德主题的讲话，通常在礼拜中宣讲。它对准的是良知，而不是课程内容。

entries.definition: a formal or official rebuke. It is usually shorter and more procedural than a lecture, which explains and moralizes at length.
entries.definitionCN: 正式或官方的斥责。它通常比 lecture 短、更讲程序，而 lecture 会长篇解释并说教。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: legere 'read', its past participle lectus, and the English family lectern, legible, legend and lesson.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词与真实同族词：legere“读”、它的过去分词 lectus，以及英语中的 lectern、legible、legend、lesson。

normal.en: legere 'to read' gives the lect- stem; lecture is literally 'a reading' before it is a talk.
normal.cn: legere“读”给出 lect- 这个词干；lecture 字面上就是“一次阅读”，之后才成为“讲座”。

normal.en: lectern, legible, legend and lesson all come from the same 'read / pick out' family, so the reading image is still visible around lecture.
normal.cn: lectern、legible、legend、lesson 都出自同一个“读／拣出”词族，因此“阅读”的意象在 lecture 周围仍然看得见。

normal.en: The old sense 'a reading' explains why a lecture was once something read aloud rather than freely spoken.
normal.cn: 古义“一次阅读”解释了为什么 lecture 早先是“朗读出来的东西”，而不是即兴讲话。

normal.en: lecture notes and lecture hall keep the classroom frame: notes record the talk, the hall houses it.
normal.cn: lecture notes 与 lecture hall 保留着课堂框架：笔记记录讲授，讲堂容纳讲授。

normal.en: give somebody a lecture moves the same talk from teaching to correcting, which is why the verb can mean 'scold'.
normal.cn: give somebody a lecture 把同一场讲话从“教”移到“纠正”，所以动词可以表示“训斥”。

abstract.en: Picture a page under a lamp: letters are picked out one by one, then the same words are spoken to rows of listeners. Lecture is that page becoming a voice.
abstract.cn: 想象台灯下的一页纸：字母被一个个拣出来，随后同一串词被念给一排排听众。lecture 就是那页纸变成声音的过程。

abstract.en: The voice can teach or scold; only the listener's posture changes — a notebook open, or a head held down.
abstract.cn: 同一个声音可以教人，也可以训人；变的只是听者的姿态——要么摊开笔记本，要么低着头。

abstract.en: A lecture is a text that has learned to stand up and speak, and a course is a row of such texts standing in line.
abstract.cn: 一场 lecture 是一段学会站起来说话的文字，而一门课程就是这样的文字排成一列。

examples.en: The lecture on volcanoes was full of photographs from the 1980 eruption.
examples.cn: 那场关于火山的讲座满是 1980 年喷发的照片。

examples.en: He lectures to first-year students three mornings a week.
examples.cn: 他每周有三个上午给一年级学生授课。

examples.en: My mother lectured me for twenty minutes about the unpaid bill.
examples.cn: 母亲为那张没付的账单训了我二十分钟。

dict_mnemonic.text: “来课扯”——上课时把内容扯成一大段 → lecture 讲座、训斥

root: 拉丁语 legere“读”（本义“采集、挑选”）→ 中世纪拉丁 lectura“阅读”，核心是“把文字拣出来、念给人听”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of lecture, one movement: a text is picked out and read, the reading becomes a talk, the talk becomes a course unit and a script, and finally the same instructive voice turns into a scolding.
sensesIntro.cn: lecture 的八个义项是一条运动线：文字被拣出来读，读变成讲授，讲授变成课时与讲稿，最后同一种“教导口吻”变成训斥。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: words are picked out of a page and spoken to people who came to listen.
core.cn: 核心意象：把字从纸页上拣出来，念给前来听的人。

branches.en: READING: the oldest layer, when lecture names the act of reading rather than a talk.
branches.cn: 阅读：最古老的一层，此时 lecture 指的是“读”这一行为，而不是讲座。

branches.en: INSTRUCTION: the classroom talk, the verb for giving it, and the public lecture as an event.
branches.cn: 讲授：课堂讲座、表示“讲授”的动词，以及作为活动的公开讲座。

branches.en: COURSE UNIT: the talk becomes a countable slot in a timetable and a syllabus.
branches.cn: 课时：讲座变成课表与教学大纲里可计数的一格。

branches.en: WRITTEN TEXT: the spoken words are fixed on paper as a script or a printed talk.
branches.cn: 书面文本：说出的话被固定在纸上，成为讲稿或印行的讲辞。

branches.en: CORRECTION: the instructive voice turns into a long scolding, as a noun and as a verb.
branches.cn: 纠正：教导的口吻变成长篇训斥，名词与动词都走这一支。

intro.en: Lecture is a borrowed Latin noun, not a prefixed English word. English adds only ordinary suffixes: -er for the person, -ship for the post, -ing for the activity; the noun also became a verb with no suffix at all.
intro.cn: lecture 是借入的拉丁名词，不是由英语前缀构成的词。英语只加普通后缀：-er 表人，-ship 表职位，-ing 表活动；名词还零派生成了动词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base legere 'read / pick out' has a large family. Note that lex 'law' is a different noun with a similar shape, and legare 'send, bequeath' is a different verb again.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基 legere“读／拣出”有一个很大的词族。注意 lex“法”是形似的另一个名词，legare“派出、遗赠”又是另一个动词。

items.meaning: a person who gives lectures, especially at a university
items.meaningCN: 讲师；授课者（-er 表示做该动作的人）
items.example: The lecturer paused to answer a question.
items.exampleCN: 讲师停下来回答了一个问题。

items.meaning: the post or position of a lecturer
items.meaningCN: 讲师职位；讲席（-ship 表示职位或身份）
items.example: She was appointed to a lectureship in physics.
items.exampleCN: 她获聘物理学讲师职位。

items.meaning: the activity of giving lectures
items.meaningCN: 授课；讲学（-ing 构成行为名词）
items.example: His lecturing took him to six countries.
items.exampleCN: 他的讲学让他去了六个国家。

items.meaning: to give a lecture; to scold at length
items.meaningCN: 讲授；长篇训斥（名动同形，不加后缀）
items.example: He lectures twice a week.
items.exampleCN: 他每周讲两次课。

items.meaning: to read; to pick out, gather
items.example: The verb is the root shared by lecture, lector and collect.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是 lecture、lector、collect 共有的词根。

items.meaning: read; picked out
items.example: Every English word on this stem keeps the reading image.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干上的英语词都保留“读”的意象。

items.meaning: an act or its result
items.example: It turns the act of reading into the noun lecture.
items.exampleCN: 它把“读”的动作变成名词 lecture。

items.meaning: a reader; one who reads aloud in a service
items.meaningCN: 诵读者；（礼拜中的）读经员
items.example: The lector read the passage aloud to the congregation.
items.exampleCN: 读经员向会众朗读了那段经文。

items.structure: Medieval Latin lectrum, from the stem lect-
items.meaning: a reading desk, especially in a church
items.example: She set her notes on the lectern before speaking.
items.exampleCN: 发言前她把讲稿放在讲台上。

latinEntries.meaning: able to be read; clear enough to read
latinEntries.meaningCN: 可读的；字迹清晰的（-ibilis 表“能够被……”）

latinEntries.meaning: a story handed down; originally 'things to be read' about the saints
latinEntries.meaningCN: 传说；原指关于圣徒“应被诵读的事迹”

latinEntries.meaning: a unit of teaching; originally a passage read aloud
latinEntries.meaningCN: 课；原义是“所读的一段文字”

latinEntries.meaning: to bring things together; literally 'to gather up'
latinEntries.meaningCN: 收集；字面义“把东西拣到一起”

definition_zh: 法律的；合法的；法定的；法律上有效的；法律职业的
definition_en: relating to law, allowed or required by law, valid in law, connected with the legal profession, or allowed by the rules of a game
core_image: 一部摊开的法典，页边压着印章：允许什么、要求什么，都写在上面
scene: 律所的会议室里，律师把合同翻到签字页。She pointed out that the clause was not legal in this country and had to be rewritten before anyone could sign.
sceneCN: 这里 legal 是「合法的、法律允许的」（第 2 个义项：为法律所允许）；句意：她指出这一条在本国不合法，必须改写之后才能签字。图中可辨识物件：会议室长桌、合同、签字页、法典、印章。

pos.zh: 法律的；合法的；法定的；法律上有效的；法律职业的
（美）法定尺寸纸张；法律文件（常用复数 legals）

collocations.zh: 黄色横线稿纸（法定尺寸）

derivatives.zh: 合法性；法律上的正当性

senses.title: Relating to law in general
senses.titleCN: 与法律有关的
senses.definition: connected with the law, the courts, or the system of rules a society enforces
senses.definitionCN: 与法律、法院或社会所执行的规则体系有关的
senses.example: She is studying the legal systems of two countries.
senses.exampleCN: 她在研究两个国家的法律体系。
senses.why: Legal began as the adjective of Latin lex 'law', so its widest sense simply marks anything belonging to the law as an institution.
senses.whyCN: legal 最初是拉丁语 lex“法”的形容词，因此最宽的义项只是标记“属于法律这个制度”的事物。

senses.title: Allowed by law
senses.titleCN: 合法的：法律允许的
senses.definition: permitted by law; not forbidden or criminal
senses.definitionCN: 为法律所允许的；未被禁止或不算犯罪的
senses.example: In some states it is legal to record a call you take part in.
senses.exampleCN: 在一些州，录下自己参与的通话是合法的。
senses.why: From 'belonging to law' comes 'consistent with law'. The question is no longer what law is about, but whether an act falls inside the permitted line.
senses.whyCN: 从“属于法律”引申出“符合法律”。问题不再是“法管什么”，而是一个行为是否落在被允许的界线之内。

senses.title: Required by law
senses.titleCN: 法定的：法律要求的
senses.definition: required or prescribed by law, so that not doing it is a breach
senses.definitionCN: 由法律要求或规定的，不做即构成违法或违约
senses.example: Employers have a legal duty to provide safety training.
senses.exampleCN: 雇主有提供安全培训的法定义务。
senses.why: The same boundary has a second side: what law permits it also commands. A legal duty is not optional, and the adjective shifts from permission to obligation.
senses.whyCN: 同一条界线还有另一面：法律允许的东西，也可以被法律命令。legal duty 不是可选项，形容词于是从“许可”滑向“义务”。

senses.title: Valid and enforceable in law
senses.titleCN: 法律上有效的
senses.definition: recognized as valid and enforceable by law, especially of a document, contract or claim
senses.definitionCN: 被法律认可为有效且可执行的，尤指文件、合同或主张
senses.example: The contract is not legal without both signatures.
senses.exampleCN: 没有双方签字，这份合同在法律上不生效。
senses.why: Here legal does not mean 'allowed' but 'having legal force'. A document can be legally made yet legally ineffective if a formality is missing.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 legal 不是“被允许”，而是“具有法律效力”。一份文件可以依法制作，却因缺少形式要件而在法律上无效。

senses.title: Of the legal profession
senses.titleCN: 法律职业的
senses.definition: relating to lawyers, their training, or the business of giving legal advice
senses.definitionCN: 与律师、其训练或提供法律意见的业务有关的
senses.example: He left banking for a legal career at thirty.
senses.exampleCN: 他三十岁时离开银行业，转做法律职业。
senses.why: The institution is also a trade. Legal then describes the people and practices that operate the system, not the rules themselves.
senses.whyCN: 法律这套制度同时也是一门行业。legal 于是描述运作这套制度的人与业务，而不是规则本身。

senses.title: Relating to lawsuits
senses.titleCN: 诉讼的
senses.definition: relating to court proceedings or to action taken through the courts
senses.definitionCN: 与法院程序或通过法院采取的行动有关的
senses.example: The tenants threatened legal action over the mould.
senses.exampleCN: 租户因霉斑问题威胁要采取法律诉讼。
senses.why: One branch of the system is dispute. Legal action names the step from a private quarrel to a case that a court can decide.
senses.whyCN: 这套制度的一支是争端。legal action 标记了从私人纠纷跨到“法院可以裁决的案件”的那一步。

senses.title: According to the letter of the law
senses.titleCN: 法律名义上的
senses.definition: existing or holding a status in law, even if the actual situation is different
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上存在或拥有某种身份，即使实际情况不同
senses.example: She is the legal owner, though her brother runs the farm.
senses.exampleCN: 她是法律上的所有者，尽管农场由她哥哥经营。
senses.why: Law can assign a name that reality does not match. Legal owner, legal parent and legal fiction all use the adjective to mark the official version, as opposed to the factual one.
senses.whyCN: 法律可以给出一个与现实不符的名义。legal owner、legal parent、legal fiction 都用这个形容词标记“官方版本”，以区别于事实版本。

senses.title: Allowed by the rules of a game
senses.titleCN: 规则允许的
senses.definition: allowed by the rules of a sport or game, though not necessarily by statute
senses.definitionCN: 为运动或游戏规则所允许的，而不一定涉及成文法
senses.example: The tackle was hard but legal.
senses.exampleCN: 那次擒抱很凶，但符合规则。
senses.why: The boundary image is borrowed from law: a game has its own code, and a move inside it is called legal by analogy. Here no court is involved.
senses.whyCN: 这里借用了“界线”的意象：游戏有自己的规则法典，规则内的动作被类比地称为 legal，此时并不涉及法院。

senses.title: Legal-size paper
senses.titleCN: 法定尺寸纸张
senses.definition: a US paper size of 8.5 by 14 inches, sold as legal pads and used for long documents
senses.definitionCN: 美国一种 8.5×14 英寸的纸张规格，做成黄色横线稿纸，用于较长的文书
senses.example: He drafted the will on a yellow legal pad.
senses.exampleCN: 他在黄色法定尺寸稿纸上起草了遗嘱。
senses.why: The adjective became a fixed label for a paper size once associated with legal records. This is an attributive use, not a new legal concept.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词固定成了纸张规格的标签，因为这种尺寸曾与法律文书相关。这是定语用法，并不是新的法律概念。

intro.en: Legal is a direct Latin borrowing, not a French one: English took legalis from Latin in the 15c, while loyal came through French from the same source. Its noun is lex, not legare and not licere.
intro.cn: legal 是直接借自拉丁语，而非借自法语：英语在 15 世纪直接取用 legalis；loyal 则是同一来源经法语变来的。它的名词是 lex，不是 legare，也不是 licere。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'of or pertaining to law'. It was borrowed straight from Latin legalis rather than through French.
items.cn: 最早记录于 15 世纪中期的英语，意为“与法律有关的”。它是直接从拉丁语 legalis 借入的，而不是经法语转手。

items.en: legalis 'of or belonging to the law' is formed from lex (genitive legis) 'law, statute, bill' plus -alis 'relating to'.
items.cn: legalis“属于法律的”由 lex（属格 legis）“法、法规、议案”加 -alis“与……有关的”构成。

items.en: lex is traced to PIE *leg- 'to collect, gather'. The idea may be 'that which is collected or laid down', but this semantic step is generally accepted, not documented.
items.cn: lex 被追溯到原始印欧语 *leg-“收集、采集”。其理据可能是“被收集、被放下之物”，但这一步只是一般认为是，并无文献确证。

items.en: legare 'to send, depute; bequeath' is a different verb, source of legate, legacy and allegation. Its connection with lex is source uncertain, so legal must not be treated as derived from legare.
items.cn: legare“派出、委任；遗赠”是另一个动词，是 legate、legacy、allegation 的来源。它与 lex 的联系来源不确定，因此不能把 legal 当作 legare 的派生词。

items.en: licere 'to be permitted' is a third root, the source of license. Being permitted by someone is not the same as being lawful under a statute.
items.cn: licere“被允许”是第三条词根线，是 license 的来源。被某人允许，与在成文法下合法，并不是同一件事。

items.en: Legal now covers the system, permission, obligation, validity and the profession. Loyal, legate and legacy are close relatives in form but come by different routes, so their meanings must not be merged.
items.cn: 现代 legal 覆盖法律体系、许可、义务、效力和法律职业。loyal、legate、legacy 在形式上亲近，却走了不同路线，词义不可合并。

note.en: The look-alike group mixes three neighbours: one from legere 'read', one genuinely from lex, and one from legare 'bequeath'. The near-meaning group separates permission, justification, statute and the courts.
note.cn: 形近组混入三个邻居：一个出自 legere“读”，一个确实出自 lex，一个出自 legare“遗赠”。近义组则把许可、正当性、成文法与法院区分开。

entries.definition: clear enough to read. It looks like legal but comes from legere 'to read', so it has nothing to do with law.
entries.definitionCN: 字迹清楚可读的。它形似 legal，却出自 legere“读”，与法律无关。

entries.definition: lawful or valid; also reasonable and justified. It comes from Latin legitimus, built on lex, so it is a true cousin of legal.
entries.definitionCN: 合法的、有效的；也指合情合理的。它来自以 lex 构成的拉丁语 legitimus，是 legal 真正的同族词。

entries.definition: money or property left to someone by a will. It looks legal, but it comes from legare 'bequeath', not from lex 'law'.
entries.definitionCN: 遗嘱留给某人的钱财或财产。它形似 legal，却出自 legare“遗赠”，而非 lex“法”。

entries.definition: allowed by law; not against the law. It is plainer and older than legal and often carries a moral tone that legal lacks.
entries.definitionCN: 法律允许的；不违法的。它比 legal 更朴素、更古老，常带有 legal 所缺的道德意味。

entries.definition: valid according to law or reason. Unlike legal, it can also mean 'fair and justified' outside any statute.
entries.definitionCN: 依法律或依理性有效的。与 legal 不同，它还可以指任何法规之外的事情“合理、正当”。

entries.definition: required or created by a written statute. It is narrower and more technical than legal, which covers the whole system.
entries.definitionCN: 由成文法规定或创设的。它比 legal 更窄、更技术化，因为 legal 覆盖整个法律体系。

entries.definition: relating to courts, judges, or the administration of justice. It names one branch of the system, not law as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 与法院、法官或司法有关的。它指体系中的一个分支，而不是整个法律。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: lex (genitive legis) 'law' + -alis, with legitimate, legislature and loyal in the same family. Watch the false friends legere 'read' and legare 'bequeath'.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词与真实同族词：lex（属格 legis）“法”+ -alis，同族有 legitimate、legislature、loyal。要警惕形近假朋友 legere“读”与 legare“遗赠”。

normal.en: lex, legis is the noun 'law'; legalis adds -alis 'relating to'. The core is simply 'of the law'.
normal.cn: lex、legis 是名词“法”；legalis 加上 -alis“与……有关”。核心意思就是“属于法的”。

normal.en: legitimate and legislature are built on the same lex, which is why they all carry a law meaning.
normal.cn: legitimate 与 legislature 都建在同一个 lex 上，所以它们都带“法”的含义。

normal.en: legacy comes from legare 'bequeath', not from lex. A legacy is what a will leaves, not what a statute says.
normal.cn: legacy 出自 legare“遗赠”，不是 lex。legacy 是遗嘱留下的东西，不是法规规定的条文。

normal.en: loyal is legalis after its trip through French: same source, different word. Loyalty is faithfulness, not legality.
normal.cn: loyal 是 legalis 经法语旅行后的样子：同源而异词。loyalty 是忠诚，不是合法性。

normal.en: legal age and legal duty show the two sides of the boundary: one permits, the other obliges.
normal.cn: legal age 与 legal duty 展示同一条界线的两面：一面是允许，一面是强制。

abstract.en: Picture a line drawn on a floor: inside it, everything is allowed; on the line, everything is required; outside it, nothing is recognized. Legal is the line itself, seen from any side.
abstract.cn: 想象地板上画的一条线：线内一切被允许，线上一切被要求，线外一切不被承认。legal 就是这条线本身，从哪一面看都算。

abstract.en: The same stamp can mean 'you may', 'you must' or 'this counts', depending on which document it lands on.
abstract.cn: 同一枚印章落在不同文件上，可以表示“你可以”“你必须”或“这份算数”。

abstract.en: Law has a name for things that do not exist in fact: the legal owner is a person the paper sees, not always the person the field sees.
abstract.cn: 法律会为事实上不存在的东西命名：法律上的所有者是纸面看见的人，未必是田里看见的人。

examples.en: The company sought legal advice before signing the deal.
examples.cn: 公司在签署交易前寻求法律咨询。

examples.en: Is it legal to park here after six?
examples.cn: 六点以后在这里停车合法吗？

examples.en: She was the legal owner of the flat but had never lived in it.
examples.cn: 她是这套公寓法律上的所有者，却从未住过。

dict_mnemonic.text: “李哥”——李哥办事只走正规手续 → legal 合法的、法律的

root: 拉丁语 lex（属格 legis）“法”+ -alis“与……有关的”，核心是“写在法典里、有法律依据”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of legal, all radiating from one noun, lex. A thing can belong to the law, be allowed by it, be required by it, be valid under it, be done by its professionals, or merely carry its label.
sensesIntro.cn: legal 的九个义项都从一个名词 lex 放射出来：某事物可以属于法律、被法律允许、被法律要求、在法律上有效、由法律从业者去做，或只是贴着法律的标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line written into a code, marking what is allowed, required and recognized.
core.cn: 核心意象：写进法典的一条界线，标出什么被允许、什么被要求、什么被承认。

branches.en: SYSTEM AND PROFESSION: law as an institution, and the people who operate it.
branches.cn: 体系与职业：作为制度的法律，以及运作它的人。

branches.en: PERMISSION: what statute allows, and, by analogy, what the rules of a game allow.
branches.cn: 许可：成文法允许的事，以及类比到游戏规则所允许的事。

branches.en: OBLIGATION: the other side of the boundary, where the law commands rather than permits.
branches.cn: 义务：界线的另一面，法律在这里不是允许而是命令。

branches.en: LEGAL EFFECT: validity, court action, and the official status that may differ from fact.
branches.cn: 法律效力：有效性、诉讼，以及可能与事实不同的官方身份。

branches.en: PAPER SIZE: a fixed attributive use, where the adjective labels a format rather than a legal idea.
branches.cn: 纸张规格：固定的定语用法，形容词在这里标记的是尺寸，而不是法律概念。

intro.en: Legal is a Latin adjective borrowed whole. English adds -ly for the adverb, -ity for the abstract noun, -ize for the verb, and the negative prefix il- before l.
intro.cn: legal 是整体借入的拉丁形容词。英语加 -ly 构成副词，-ity 构成抽象名词，-ize 构成动词，并在 l 前用否定前缀 il-。

latinIntro.en: The lex family is wide: legitimate, legislature, loyal and privilege all contain the law noun in different shapes. Keep it apart from legere 'read' and legare 'bequeath'.
latinIntro.cn: lex 词族很宽：legitimate、legislature、loyal、privilege 都以不同形态含有“法”这个名词。要把它与 legere“读”、legare“遗赠”分开。

items.meaning: in a way that is allowed by law; according to law
items.meaningCN: 合法地；在法律上（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The protest was legally held.
items.exampleCN: 那场抗议是合法举行的。

items.meaning: the quality or state of being legal
items.meaningCN: 合法性（-ity 构成抽象名词）
items.example: The court questioned the legality of the search.
items.exampleCN: 法院质疑那次搜查的合法性。

items.meaning: to make something legal by law
items.example: Several states have legalized recreational use.
items.exampleCN: 有几个州已将娱乐性使用合法化。

items.meaning: forbidden by law
items.meaningCN: 非法的；违法的（il- 是否定前缀，用在 l 前）
items.example: It is illegal to dump waste in the river.
items.exampleCN: 向河里倾倒废物是违法的。

items.meaning: law; a statute
items.example: The noun supplies the law at the centre of legal.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供 legal 核心的“法”。

items.meaning: law (combining form)
items.example: The stem appears in legal, legislate and legitimate.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干见于 legal、legislate 与 legitimate。

items.meaning: relating to, belonging to
items.example: It turns the noun for law into the adjective legal.
items.exampleCN: 它把“法”这个名词变成形容词 legal。

items.meaning: the quality or state of being
items.example: It forms legality, the quality of being lawful.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 legality，即合乎法律的性质。

items.meaning: strict adherence to law or to written rules
items.meaningCN: 条文主义；死守法律条文
items.example: Critics say legalism ignores the purpose behind the rule.
items.exampleCN: 批评者说条文主义忽视了规则背后的目的。

latinEntries.meaning: lawful, valid; also reasonable and justified
latinEntries.meaningCN: 合法的、有效的；也指合理正当的（词根仍是 lex“法”）

latinEntries.meaning: the body that has power to make laws
latinEntries.meaningCN: 立法机关（legis 属格 + lator“提出者”）

latinEntries.meaning: faithful to a ruler, country or promise
latinEntries.meaningCN: 忠诚的；同源于 legalis，经法语音变而成，不是英语 legal 的派生

latinEntries.meaning: a special right; originally a law made for an individual
latinEntries.meaningCN: 特权；原指为某个人制定的法律（privus“个人”+ lex“法”）

definition_zh: 立法；制定法律；以立法规定；以法律促成
definition_en: to make laws, or to establish, require or bring about something by making laws
core_image: 议会大厅里举起的手：把一条规则写进法典
scene: 深夜的议会大厅里，议员们围绕一项排放法案辩论。Parliament can legislate on emissions, and the electronic board lit up one name after another as the vote went on.
sceneCN: 这里 legislate 是「立法、制定法律」（第 1 个义项：立法机关制定法律）；句意：议会可以就排放问题立法，随着表决进行，电子牌上的名字一盏盏亮起。图中可辨识物件：议会大厅、法案文本、表决按钮、投票牌、议长席。

pos.zh: 立法；制定法律；以立法规定

collocations.zh: 为所有情况立法（常用于否定）

senses.title: Make laws as a body
senses.titleCN: 立法：由立法机关制定法律
senses.definition: to make laws, especially as a parliament or other authorized body
senses.definitionCN: 制定法律，尤指由议会或其他获授权的机构进行
senses.example: Parliament legislates for the whole country.
senses.exampleCN: 议会为全国制定法律。
senses.why: The word is built from legis lator, 'proposer of a law'. The verb names the core activity of that person and that body: turning a proposal into binding law.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 legis lator“法律的提出者”构成。动词指的就是那个人、那个机构的核心活动：把提案变成有约束力的法律。

senses.title: Establish something by statute
senses.titleCN: 以立法规定某事
senses.definition: to establish, require, or create something by passing a law
senses.definitionCN: 通过立法确立、要求或创设某事
senses.example: The state legislated a cap on rent increases.
senses.exampleCN: 该州通过立法给租金上涨设了上限。
senses.why: Here the verb takes a direct object: the thing that the law creates. The focus moves from the lawmaking body to the result written into the statute.
senses.whyCN: 这里动词带直接宾语，即法律所创设的东西。焦点从立法机构移到写进法条的那个结果。

senses.title: Make laws about a subject
senses.titleCN: 就某领域立法
senses.definition: to make laws dealing with a particular subject or area of activity
senses.definitionCN: 就某一主题或活动领域制定法律
senses.example: The assembly legislated on land use for three years.
senses.exampleCN: 议会就土地用途立了三年法。
senses.why: With on or for, the verb marks its territory. The law is not named; the field it covers is, which is how committees and ministries talk about their work.
senses.whyCN: 接 on 或 for 时，动词标出的是“领地”。被点名的不是某条法，而是它覆盖的领域，委员会和部委常用这种说法。

senses.title: Make laws to prohibit or promote
senses.titleCN: 立法禁止或促进
senses.definition: to make laws in order to forbid something or to encourage it
senses.definitionCN: 为禁止某事或鼓励某事而制定法律
senses.example: Many countries have legislated against single-use plastics.
senses.exampleCN: 许多国家已立法禁止一次性塑料制品。
senses.why: Against and for add direction: the law is now a tool aimed at an outcome, either pushing an activity out or pulling it in.
senses.whyCN: against 与 for 加上了方向：法律成了一件对准某个结果工具，要么把某种行为推出去，要么把它拉进来。

senses.title: Exercise lawmaking power
senses.titleCN: 行使立法权
senses.definition: of a parliament or assembly, to use its constitutional power to make laws
senses.definitionCN: 指议会或代表大会行使其宪法赋予的立法权力
senses.example: The assembly has no power to legislate in criminal matters.
senses.exampleCN: 该议会无权在刑事事项上立法。
senses.why: This sense is about competence rather than output: the question is whether the body is allowed to legislate at all, not what it decides to pass.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项谈的是“权限”而不是“产物”：问题在于该机构究竟有没有立法资格，而不在于它决定通过什么。

senses.title: Bring about a result by law
senses.titleCN: 以立法促成某种结果
senses.definition: to try to produce a social result by passing laws, often with the implication that law alone may not succeed
senses.definitionCN: 试图通过立法产生某种社会结果，常暗示单靠法律未必成功
senses.example: You cannot legislate equality into existence overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 你不可能靠一夜立法就造出平等。
senses.why: The verb extends from lawmaking to engineering society. The object is now an abstract condition, and the usual tone is skeptical: statutes can command, but cannot change hearts.
senses.whyCN: 动词从“制定法律”扩展到“设计社会”。宾语变成抽象状况，语气通常带怀疑：法令可以命令，却改不了人心。

senses.title: Lay down rules inside an organization
senses.titleCN: 在组织内部制定规则
senses.definition: to set rules for behaviour within an organization or activity, without any formal statute
senses.definitionCN: 为组织或活动内部的行为设定规则，不涉及正式成文法
senses.example: The committee legislated a dress code for staff.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会为员工制定了着装规定。
senses.why: Any rule-making body can be described by analogy as legislating. The word lends gravity to ordinary internal rules, and no parliament is involved.
senses.whyCN: 任何制定规则的机构都可以被类比地说成 legislate。这个词给普通的内部规定添了分量，实际并无议会参与。

senses.title: Provide for every case by law
senses.titleCN: 为一切情况立法（多用于否定）
senses.definition: to cover every possible case by law, used especially in negative statements about the limits of legislation
senses.definitionCN: 用法律覆盖一切可能情况，尤用于否定句，说明立法的边界
senses.example: You can't legislate for bad luck.
senses.exampleCN: 人没法为倒霉立法。
senses.why: This is the boundary sense. The verb is used in the negative to mark what statutes cannot reach: accident, taste, chance and human nature.
senses.whyCN: 这是边界义项。动词用在否定句里，标出成文法够不到的地方：意外、品味、运气与人性。

intro.en: Legislate is a back-formation from legislation, and legislation is Latin legis lator, 'proposer of a law'. The second element is lator, from ferre 'to carry', not legare 'to send'.
intro.cn: legislate 是从 legislation 逆构出来的，而 legislation 来自拉丁语 legis lator“法律的提出者”。第二个成分是 lator，出自 ferre“携带”，不是 legare“派出”。

items.en: First recorded as an English verb in the 1710s, made by dropping -ion from legislation. This is a back-formation, not a word inherited from Latin.
items.cn: 作为英语动词最早记录于 18 世纪初，由 legislation 去掉 -ion 逆构而成。它是逆构词，不是从拉丁语直接继承的词。

items.en: legislation is recorded in English from the 1650s, from Late Latin legislationem, a noun of action from legislator.
items.cn: legislation 在英语中见于 17 世纪中期，来自晚期拉丁语 legislationem，是 legislator 的行为名词。

items.en: legislator is literally legis lator, 'proposer or bearer of a law'. lator is an agent noun from latus, the suppletive past participle of ferre 'to carry'.
items.cn: legislator 字面上是 legis lator“法律的提出者或携带者”。lator 是由 latus 构成的施动名词，而 latus 是 ferre“携带”的替补过去分词。

items.en: The first element is lex (genitive legis) 'law'. The compound says 'one who brings a law', not 'one who delegates'. Its deeper tie to PIE *leg- 'gather' is generally accepted.
items.cn: 第一个成分是 lex（属格 legis）“法”。这个复合词说的是“带来法律的人”，不是“委派的人”。它与原始印欧语 *leg-“采集”的更深联系属于一般认为是。

items.en: legare 'to send, depute; bequeath' is a separate verb (legate, legacy, allegation). The common claim that lex comes from legare is source uncertain, so the two must not be conflated.
items.cn: legare“派出、委任；遗赠”是另一个动词（legate、legacy、allegation）。认为 lex 来自 legare 的常见说法来源不确定，两者不能混为一谈。

items.en: Legislate remains the formal verb of institutions; everyday English says pass or make a law. Legislation, legislative, legislator and legislature keep the Latin compound visible.
items.cn: 现代英语中 legislate 仍是机构的正式动词，日常则说 pass a law 或 make a law。legislation、legislative、legislator、legislature 让这个拉丁复合词的结构仍然可见。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the legis- shape through its derived forms and one false neighbour. The near-meaning group separates the whole act of legislating from its single procedural steps.
note.cn: 形近组沿着 legis- 这一形，梳理派生形式与一个假邻居；近义组把“立法”这一整体行为与其单个程序步骤分开。

entries.definition: the process of making laws, or the laws made. It is the noun from which legislate was back-formed.
entries.definitionCN: 立法过程，或所制定的法律。它正是 legislate 逆构所依据的名词。

entries.definition: a person who makes laws; a member of a legislature. The -or marks the person, while legislate marks the activity.
entries.definitionCN: 立法者；立法机关的成员。-or 标记人，而 legislate 标记活动。

entries.definition: lawful, valid, or justified. It shares the legis- look and the lex root, but it means 'conforming to law', not 'making law'.
entries.definitionCN: 合法的、有效的或正当的。它同样有 legis- 的外形和 lex 词根，但意思是“符合法律”，不是“制定法律”。

entries.definition: to make a law officially. It focuses on the moment a bill becomes law, while legislate covers the whole activity.
entries.definitionCN: 正式制定法律。它聚焦于议案成为法律的那一刻，而 legislate 覆盖整个立法活动。

entries.definition: to approve a bill by vote. It names one step in the process, not the whole lawmaking function.
entries.definitionCN: 通过投票批准议案。它指过程中的一步，而不是整个立法职能。

entries.definition: to order something by authority, often by a ruler or executive. It does not require a legislature.
entries.definitionCN: 由权威（常是统治者或行政机关）下令。它不需要立法机关。

entries.definition: to control an activity by rules or supervision. It is broader and can be done by agencies without new legislation.
entries.definitionCN: 用规则或监管控制某项活动。它更宽，可由机构在没有新立法的情况下实施。

normalIntro.en: Real parts: legis 'of law' + lator 'proposer / bearer', with lator from latus, the past participle of ferre 'carry'. The verb itself is a back-formation from legislation.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词：legis“法律的”+ lator“提出者／携带者”，而 lator 出自 ferre“携带”的过去分词 latus。动词本身是从 legislation 逆构来的。

normal.en: legis lator = 'law-carrier': a legislator is someone who brings a law forward, and legislate is what that person does.
normal.cn: legis lator＝“带着法律的人”：立法者就是把法律提出来的人，legislate 就是这个人做的事。

normal.en: lator is built on latus, the past participle of ferre 'to carry' — the same verb behind transfer, refer and relate.
normal.cn: lator 建在 latus 上，而 latus 是 ferre“携带”的过去分词——也是 transfer、refer、relate 背后的那个动词。

normal.en: The verb is a back-formation: legislation came first, and English cut off -ion to get legislate.
normal.cn: 这个动词是逆构词：先有 legislation，英语再砍掉 -ion 得到 legislate。

normal.en: legislate on a subject, legislate against an activity, legislate something into law: the prepositions show law as a field, a fence or a pen.
normal.cn: legislate on 某主题、legislate against 某活动、legislate something into law：介词把法律呈现为领域、围栏或写入的笔。

normal.en: You can't legislate for bad luck: the negative use marks the edge of what statutes can control.
normal.cn: you can't legislate for bad luck：否定用法标出成文法所能控制的边界。

abstract.en: Picture a hand carrying a sheet of rules across a hall and laying it on a table: the hand is lator, the sheet is lex, and the walk is the legislating.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手举着一页规则穿过大厅，把它放到桌上：手是 lator，纸页是 lex，走这一趟就是 legislating。

abstract.en: A law is a line drawn for everyone at once; legislating is the moment the pen decides where the line goes.
abstract.cn: 法律是一条同时画给所有人的线；legislating 就是笔决定这条线画在哪里的那一刻。

abstract.en: The same pen can build a wall, open a door, or try to write a feeling into the code. The last attempt is where the word turns skeptical.
abstract.cn: 同一支笔可以筑墙、开门，也可以试着把一种情感写进法典；最后这种尝试正是这个词转为怀疑的地方。

examples.en: The province legislated new limits on water use last spring.
examples.cn: 该省去年春天通过立法对用水设了新的限制。

examples.en: It is not the court's job to legislate from the bench.
examples.cn: 从法官席上立法并不是法院的职责。

examples.en: No assembly can legislate away a drought.
examples.cn: 任何议会都无法用立法消除旱情。

dict_mnemonic.text: “来这立”——来这儿立一条规矩 → legislate 立法

root: 拉丁语 legis lator“法律的提出者”= lex“法”+ lator（ferre“携带”的替补过去分词 latus 所派生的施动名词），核心是“把法条写进法典”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of legislate, from the body that makes law to the single thing a law creates, then to the fields, prohibitions, organizations and limits that law tries to cover.
sensesIntro.cn: legislate 的八个义项，从“立法机关制定法律”到“法律所创设的某一件事”，再到法律试图覆盖的领域、禁令、组织与边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand carries a rule to the code and writes it in as law.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把一条规则带到法典前，把它写成法律。

branches.en: LAWMAKING POWER: the institution's core act and its constitutional competence to perform it.
branches.cn: 立法权：机构的核心行为，以及它履行该行为的宪法权限。

branches.en: ENACT A RESULT: a statute creates something, and the same verb extends to producing social results.
branches.cn: 以法促成：法条创设某物，同一个动词又延伸到产生社会结果。

branches.en: SUBJECT MATTER: the field the law covers, and the direction it pushes that field in.
branches.cn: 规制领域：法律覆盖的领域，以及它把该领域推向的方向。

branches.en: ORGANIZATIONAL RULES: rule-making by analogy inside bodies that are not parliaments.
branches.cn: 组织规则：类比地用于非议会机构内部的规则制定。

branches.en: LIMIT OF LAW: the negative idiom marks what statutes cannot provide for.
branches.cn: 法律的边界：否定习语标出成文法无法规定的东西。

intro.en: Legislate is a back-formed verb, so its English family is mostly nouns and adjectives built on legislation and legislator: -ion, -ive, -or, -ure.
intro.cn: legislate 是逆构动词，因此它的英语词族主要是建在 legislation 与 legislator 上的名词和形容词：-ion、-ive、-or、-ure。

latinIntro.en: The Latin pieces are legis 'of law' plus lator or latio, both from latus, the past participle of ferre 'to carry'. This is the 'carry' family, not the legare 'send' family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁成分是 legis“法律的”加 lator 或 latio，二者都出自 ferre“携带”的过去分词 latus。这是“携带”词族，不是 legare“派出”词族。

items.meaning: the making of laws; the laws produced
items.meaningCN: 立法；所制定的法律（-ion 构成名词）
items.example: The legislation passed after a long debate.
items.exampleCN: 这项立法经过长时间辩论后获得通过。

items.meaning: having the power or function of making laws
items.meaningCN: 立法的；有立法权的（-ive 构成形容词）
items.example: The assembly has legislative authority over taxes.
items.exampleCN: 该议会对税收拥有立法权。

items.meaning: a person who makes laws
items.meaningCN: 立法者；议员（-or 表示人）
items.example: The bill was drafted by a senior legislator.
items.exampleCN: 这项议案由一位资深议员起草。

items.meaning: the body of people with power to make laws
items.meaningCN: 立法机关（-ure 表示机构）
items.example: The state legislature meets for three months each year.
items.exampleCN: 州立法机关每年开会三个月。

items.meaning: law (combining form)
items.example: The form joins law to the verb of carrying.
items.exampleCN: 这个形式把“法”与“携带”的动词连起来。

items.structure: past-participial stem of Latin ferre 'to carry'
items.meaning: carried, brought forward
items.example: The stem marks the law as something carried into effect.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干把法律标为被携带生效之物。

items.meaning: to make, to act
items.example: It turns the law-bearing phrase into the verb legislate.
items.exampleCN: 它把“承载法律”的词组变成动词 legislate。

items.meaning: a bearer; one who brings a bill forward
items.example: In Latin the lator is the one who carries a measure to the assembly.
items.exampleCN: 在拉丁语里，lator 指把议案带到议会的人。

latinEntries.meaning: the bringing forward of a law; lawmaking
latinEntries.meaningCN: 法律的提出；立法（latio 是 ferre 家族的行为名词）

latinEntries.meaning: of or for making laws
latinEntries.meaningCN: 立法的；立法性质的

latinEntries.meaning: one who proposes or carries a law
latinEntries.meaningCN: 立法者；字面“提出法律的人”

latinEntries.meaning: a bearer, a one who carries or brings
latinEntries.meaningCN: 携带者；提出者（拉丁语词干，不是英语独立常用词）

definition_zh: 自由主义的；开明的；慷慨的；宽松的；人文学科的
definition_en: open to different views, favouring political reform, generous in amount, not strict or literal, or relating to a broad education in the arts and sciences
core_image: 一个不被绳索束缚的人，伸手把东西分给别人
scene: 社区听证会上，一位议员支持为低收入家庭增建住房。The liberal member spoke for more low-income housing and argued that the planning rules should be looser.
sceneCN: 这里 liberal 是「政治立场偏自由派、支持改革的」（第 2 个义项：政治上的自由主义）；句意：这位自由派议员支持为低收入家庭增建住房，并主张规划规则应当更宽松。图中可辨识物件：听证会标牌、麦克风、住房规划图、选民登记表。

pos.zh: 自由主义的；开明的；慷慨的；宽松的；人文教育的
自由主义者；自由派支持者

senses.title: Open to different views
senses.titleCN: 开明的：能容纳不同意见
senses.definition: willing to accept and tolerate behaviour or opinions different from one's own
senses.definitionCN: 愿意接受并容忍与自己不同的行为或观点
senses.example: Her parents were liberal about curfews, as long as she called home.
senses.exampleCN: 她父母对宵禁时间很开明，只要她打电话回家就行。
senses.why: The core is Latin liber 'free'. A liberal mind is not bound by a narrow rule or prejudice; it leaves room for what it did not expect.
senses.whyCN: 核心是拉丁语 liber“自由的”。开明的头脑不被狭窄的规矩或偏见捆住，会为意料之外的东西留出空间。

senses.title: Politically reform-minded
senses.titleCN: 政治上的自由派
senses.definition: favouring social reform, individual rights and government action, often associated with the centre-left
senses.definitionCN: 支持社会改革、个人权利与政府作为，常与中左政治立场相关
senses.example: The liberal party lost its rural seats in the election.
senses.exampleCN: 自由派政党在选举中失去了乡村选区。
senses.why: In 19c politics liberal meant free from arbitrary rule and favouring constitutional government. The label later shifted toward social reform, and its meaning still varies by country.
senses.whyCN: 在 19 世纪政治中，liberal 指免于专断统治、支持宪政。这个标签后来偏向社会改革，其含义至今因国家而异。

senses.title: Generous in amount
senses.titleCN: 充足的：分量慷慨
senses.definition: given or existing in large amounts; more than enough
senses.definitionCN: 给予或存在的量大；足够而有余
senses.example: Add a liberal amount of olive oil before roasting.
senses.exampleCN: 烤之前加足量的橄榄油。
senses.why: Latin liberalis already meant 'generous, munificent'. The free man was expected to give freely, so the adjective moved from social status to quantity.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 liberalis 本就有“慷慨、大方”之义。自由人被认为应当大方给予，于是形容词从社会身份滑到了数量。

senses.title: Not strictly literal
senses.titleCN: 不作字面拘泥的
senses.definition: not strictly literal or exact; allowing freedom in interpretation or wording
senses.definitionCN: 不严格依照字面或精确表述；在解释或措辞上留出自由
senses.example: The translator took a liberal reading of the poem's last line.
senses.exampleCN: 译者对诗的最后一行作了较自由的解读。
senses.why: Freedom applies to wording: a liberal translation or interpretation departs from the letter in order to keep the sense.
senses.whyCN: 自由落在措辞上：liberal translation 或 interpretation 离开字面，为的是保住意思。

senses.title: Of a broad education in the arts
senses.titleCN: 博雅教育的：人文学科的
senses.definition: relating to a broad education in humanities, social sciences and sciences rather than narrow technical training
senses.definitionCN: 与人文、社会科学和自然科学的广博教育有关，而非狭窄的技术训练
senses.example: He studied liberal arts before law school.
senses.exampleCN: 他在法学院之前读的是人文学科。
senses.why: artes liberales were the skills befitting a free citizen, as opposed to a slave or a tradesman. Liberal arts still names that ideal of a broad, non-vocational education.
senses.whyCN: artes liberales 是“配得上自由公民的技艺”，区别于奴隶或工匠的技能。liberal arts 至今指这种广博而非职业化的教育理想。

senses.title: Noun: a person of liberal views
senses.titleCN: 名词：自由派人士
senses.definition: a person who holds liberal political or social views
senses.definitionCN: 持自由派政治或社会观点的人
senses.example: The bill split the liberals in the senate.
senses.exampleCN: 这项议案让参议院里的自由派分裂了。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a countable noun by metonymy: a person is named by the position they hold. Politics is the usual setting for this use.
senses.whyCN: 形容词通过转喻变成可数名词：用一个人所持的立场来指这个人。这种用法通常出现在政治语境。

senses.title: Free-market economics
senses.titleCN: 经济上的自由市场主张
senses.definition: favouring free markets, private ownership and little state control, in the classical economic sense
senses.definitionCN: 在古典经济学意义上支持自由市场、私有制与较少的国家控制
senses.example: The party is liberal on trade but cautious on welfare.
senses.exampleCN: 该党在贸易上主张自由，在福利上却谨慎。
senses.why: Classical liberalism put economic freedom alongside political freedom. Note the trap: in US politics 'liberal' often means the opposite on economic policy, so the sense depends on context.
senses.whyCN: 古典自由主义把经济自由与政治自由并列。注意陷阱：在美国政治语境中，liberal 在经济政策上常指相反方向，因此词义要看上下文。

senses.title: Liberal with: giving freely
senses.titleCN: 对某物出手大方
senses.definition: generous in giving something to other people, sometimes to the point of excess
senses.definitionCN: 在给予他人某物时很大方，有时到了过分的程度
senses.example: He was liberal with praise and stingy with details.
senses.exampleCN: 他夸人毫不吝啬，给细节却很小气。
senses.why: Here the quantity sense is directed at people. Liberal with praise means the giving hand opens wide; the same phrase can quietly criticize someone who gives too freely.
senses.whyCN: 这里数量义对准了人。liberal with praise 意味着给予的手张得很开；同一短语也可以暗含批评，指某人给得过头。

senses.title: Not strict: allowing latitude
senses.titleCN: 宽松的：执行不严的
senses.definition: not strictly enforced or tightly controlled; allowing freedom of action
senses.definitionCN: 不被严格执行或 tightly 控制；允许行动自由
senses.example: The school has a liberal policy on mobile phones.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校对手机的规定很宽松。
senses.why: The freedom is now built into an arrangement, not into a person's mind. A liberal policy leaves the margin wide, which is why the word can describe rules as well as people.
senses.whyCN: 这时自由被写进了安排本身，而不是某人的头脑。宽松的政策把余地留得很宽，因此这个词既能形容人，也能形容规则。

intro.en: Liberal comes from Latin liber 'free', not from liber 'book'. Its oldest English sense was 'generous, noble', and 'free' ran through both the social and the educational branches.
intro.cn: liberal 出自拉丁语 liber“自由的”，不是 liber“书”。它最早的英语义是“慷慨、高贵”，而“自由”贯穿了社会与教育这两条分支。

items.en: First recorded in English meaning 'generous, noble, free', especially of a person of high birth or a free citizen.
items.cn: 最早记录于 14 世纪中期的英语，意为“慷慨的、高贵的、自由的”，尤指出身高贵者或自由公民。

items.en: liberalis 'of a free person, noble, generous, munificent' is formed from liber 'free' plus -alis.
items.cn: liberalis“属于自由人的、高贵的、慷慨的”由 liber“自由的”加 -alis 构成。

items.en: liber 'free' and liber 'book' are two different nouns. Library comes from librarium 'bookcase', built on liber 'book / inner bark', so library is not a relative of liberal.
items.cn: liber“自由的”与 liber“书”是两个不同的名词。library 出自 librarium“书柜”，建在 liber“书／树内皮”上，因此 library 不是 liberal 的亲戚。

items.en: artes liberales were 'the arts befitting a free person', the broad curriculum of grammar, rhetoric, logic, arithmetic, geometry, music and astronomy. English liberal arts is a calque of that phrase.
items.cn: artes liberales 是“配得上自由人的技艺”，包括语法、修辞、逻辑、算术、几何、音乐与天文这一广博课程。英语 liberal arts 就是该短语的仿译。

items.en: liber is connected with PIE *leudh- 'free, grow' (some sources gloss it 'people'). This reconstruction is generally accepted rather than certain.
items.cn: liber 与原始印欧语 *leudh-“自由、成长”相联系（也有资料解作“人民”）。这一重构属于一般认为是，并非确证。

items.en: The political sense develops in the 19c around constitutional government and free trade. In 20c US English liberal came to mean social reform and state action, which is why the word can sound opposite in different countries. It is never related to licere 'be permitted' (license).
items.cn: 政治义在 19 世纪围绕宪政与自由贸易发展起来。到 20 世纪美国英语中，liberal 转指社会改革与国家作为，因此这个词在不同国家听起来可能相反。它与 licere“被允许”（license）从无关系。

note.en: The look-alike group turns on the two different Latins: liber 'free' gives liberty, liberate and liberal, while liber 'book' gives library. The near-meaning group separates the political label from attitude and amount words.
note.cn: 形近组的关键是两个不同的拉丁词：liber“自由的”给出 liberty、liberate、liberal，而 liber“书”给出 library。近义组把政治标签与态度词、数量词分开。

entries.definition: freedom from control or restriction. It is the abstract noun of liber 'free', the same source as liberal.
entries.definitionCN: 免于控制或限制的自由。它是 liber“自由的”的抽象名词，与 liberal 同源。

entries.definition: to set someone free from control, prison or occupation. It is the verb from liberare, the same 'free' family.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人摆脱控制、监禁或占领。它出自 liberare，属于同一个“自由”词族。

entries.definition: a place where books are kept. It looks like liberal, but it comes from liber 'book / inner bark' through librarium, not from liber 'free'.
entries.definitionCN: 藏书的地方。它形似 liberal，却出自 liber“书／树内皮”经 librarium 演变，不是 liber“自由的”。

entries.definition: favouring reform or new ideas, often more activist than liberal. It is a political label, not a word for generosity or education.
entries.definitionCN: 支持改革或新观念的，通常比 liberal 更行动派。它是政治标签，不表示慷慨或教育。

entries.definition: willing to accept differences. It names the attitude itself and carries no political programme.
entries.definitionCN: 愿意接受差异的。它只指态度本身，不携带政治纲领。

entries.definition: giving much or containing much. It overlaps liberal in amount and giving, but has no political or educational sense.
entries.definitionCN: 给予很多或含量充足的。它在数量与给予义上与 liberal 重叠，但没有政治或教育义。

entries.definition: willing to consider new ideas. It is more personal and less ideological than liberal.
entries.definitionCN: 愿意考虑新观念的。它比 liberal 更个人化，意识形态色彩更弱。

normalIntro.en: Real parts: liber 'free' + -alis, with liberty, liberate and deliver in the same family. The look-alike library belongs to liber 'book' and must be kept apart.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词：liber“自由的”+ -alis，同族有 liberty、liberate、deliver。形近的 library 属于 liber“书”，必须分开。

normal.en: liber 'free' is the stem: liberal, liberty, liberate and deliver all carry some form of 'freeing'.
normal.cn: liber“自由的”是词干：liberal、liberty、liberate、deliver 都带有某种“使自由”的意思。

normal.en: artes liberales were the skills of a free citizen, which is why liberal arts means a broad education rather than a political opinion.
normal.cn: artes liberales 是自由公民的技艺，所以 liberal arts 指广博教育，而不是政治观点。

normal.en: library comes from liber 'book', a different noun. A library is a book-place, not a freedom-place.
normal.cn: library 出自另一个名词 liber“书”。图书馆是放书的地方，不是放自由的地方。

normal.en: deliver is de- 'away' + liberare 'free': to deliver a parcel is to free it from your hands into someone else's.
normal.cn: deliver 是 de-“离开”+ liberare“使自由”：把包裹交付出去，就是让它离开你的手、到别人手里。

normal.en: liberal with praise uses the generosity branch, not the political one: the hand gives freely.
normal.cn: liberal with praise 走的是“慷慨”分支，不是政治分支：手在大方地给。

abstract.en: Picture a gate with no lock: a person can walk out, and because they can walk out, they can also leave room for others to walk in. Liberal is that unlocked gate, applied to minds, rules and money.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇没有锁的门：人能走出去，也正因为能走出去，才会给别人留出走进来的余地。liberal 就是这扇没锁的门，用在头脑、规则与金钱上。

abstract.en: Freedom can be spent in three directions: given away as generosity, kept open as tolerance, or written into a curriculum as the education of a free person.
abstract.cn: 自由可以花在三个方向：作为慷慨被给出去，作为宽容被留开，或作为自由人的教育被写进课程。

abstract.en: The same word can mean 'leave it loose' and 'give a lot'. Both are the image of a hand that does not close.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既可以指“放宽”，也可以指“给得多”。两者都是同一幅图：一只不握紧的手。

examples.en: A liberal education taught her to question her own assumptions.
examples.cn: 博雅教育教会她质疑自己的预设。

examples.en: Pour a liberal amount of sauce over the fish.
examples.cn: 在鱼上浇足量的酱汁。

examples.en: He is socially liberal but fiscally conservative.
examples.cn: 他在社会议题上开明，在财政上保守。

dict_mnemonic.text: “离不了”——离不了自由，凡事主张放开 → liberal 自由的、开明的

root: 拉丁语 liber“自由的”（不是 liber“书”）+ -alis，核心是“不受束缚的、像自由人那样给予”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of liberal, all variations on 'not bound': a mind not bound by prejudice, a politics of reform, a hand that gives widely, a reading not bound to the letter, an education for a free person, and rules left loose.
sensesIntro.cn: liberal 的九个义项都是“不受束缚”的变体：不被偏见捆住的头脑、改革的政治、给得宽的手、不囿于字面的解读、自由人的教育，以及留得很松的规则。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an unbound person, whose hand is free to give and whose mind is free to admit.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个未被捆住的人，手可以自由给予，头脑可以自由接纳。

branches.en: OPEN AND LOOSE: the same freedom applied to a mind and to a set of rules.
branches.cn: 开明与宽松：同一种自由，用在头脑上，也用在规则上。

branches.en: POLITICS AND ECONOMY: the reform label, the person who wears it, and the free-market branch.
branches.cn: 政治与经济：改革标签、持标签的人，以及自由市场分支。

branches.en: GENEROSITY: abundance in amount, and the open hand that gives to people.
branches.cn: 慷慨：数量上的充足，以及向人张开的手。

branches.en: INTERPRETATION: freedom from the literal letter in reading and translation.
branches.cn: 解释：在阅读与翻译中摆脱字面的束缚。

branches.en: EDUCATION: artes liberales, the broad curriculum of a free person.
branches.cn: 教育：artes liberales，自由人的广博课程。

intro.en: Liberal takes ordinary English suffixes: -ly for the adverb, -ism for the system, -ize for the verb, and il- as a negative prefix before l.
intro.cn: liberal 接的是普通英语后缀：-ly 构成副词，-ism 构成主义，-ize 构成动词，il- 则在 l 前作否定前缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family of liber 'free' includes liberty, liberate, deliver and libertine. Library belongs to the other liber, 'book', and is not part of this family.
latinIntro.cn: liber“自由的”这一拉丁词族包括 liberty、liberate、deliver、libertine。library 属于另一个 liber“书”，不在这个词族里。

items.meaning: generously, in large amounts, or in an open-minded way
items.meaningCN: 慷慨地；大量地；开明地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: Apply the cream liberally to the burned area.
items.exampleCN: 在烫伤处大量涂抹药膏。

items.meaning: the political and economic doctrine of liberal ideas
items.meaningCN: 自由主义（-ism 构成主义、学说）
items.example: Classical liberalism favoured free trade.
items.exampleCN: 古典自由主义支持自由贸易。

items.meaning: to make rules or systems less strict
items.meaningCN: 使自由化；放宽（-ize 表示“使……”）
items.example: The government liberalized the visa rules.
items.exampleCN: 政府放宽了签证规定。

items.meaning: not tolerant of different views; opposed to liberal ideas
items.meaningCN: 不宽容的；反自由的（il- 是否定前缀）
items.example: The ban was criticized as illiberal.
items.exampleCN: 这项禁令被批评为不宽容。

items.meaning: free; not enslaved
items.example: The adjective sits at the centre of liberal and liberty.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是 liberal 与 liberty 的共同核心。

items.meaning: relating to
items.example: It carries the free adjective into English as liberal.
items.exampleCN: 它把“自由”这个形容词带进英语成为 liberal。

items.structure: suffix naming a system or movement
items.meaning: a body of doctrine or practice
items.example: It forms liberalism, the political doctrine.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 liberalism 这一政治学说。

items.meaning: quality or state
items.example: It forms liberality, the quality of being generous or open.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 liberality，即慷慨或开明的品质。

items.meaning: to set free
items.example: The army liberated the city at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 军队在黎明时解放了这座城市。

latinEntries.meaning: freedom from control or restriction
latinEntries.meaningCN: 自由；免于控制（-tas 构成抽象名词，经法语入英语）

latinEntries.meaning: to set someone or something free
latinEntries.meaningCN: 解放；使自由（出自 liberare“使自由”）

latinEntries.meaning: to hand over, save, or set free; literally 'to free away'
latinEntries.meaningCN: 交付；解救；字面“使脱离而自由”（de- + liberare）

latinEntries.meaning: a person without moral restraint; originally a freed slave
latinEntries.meaningCN: 放荡者；原指被释放的奴隶（自由义走偏为“无约束”）

definition_zh: 许可；许可证；执照；正式批准；授权使用
definition_en: official permission to do something, the document that proves it, or the act of granting such permission
core_image: 权威递出的一把钥匙：门原本锁着，得到许可的人才能推开
scene: 市政厅窗口前，申请人接过盖了钢印的执照。The clerk handed over the business license, and the applicant put it in the same folder as her driving permit.
sceneCN: 这里 license 是「官方许可证」，也落在纸质证件这一层（第 1、2 个义项：官方许可；证明许可的证件）；句意：工作人员递过营业执照，申请人把它和驾驶证一起放进文件夹。图中可辨识物件：市政厅窗口、盖钢印的执照、文件夹、驾照。

pos.zh: 许可证；执照；许可；自由、放纵（古义/文学）
正式批准；给……发许可证；授权使用

collocations.zh: 经许可（授权生产或使用）
诗的破格；艺术上的自由处理

derivatives.zh: 许可的颁发；执业许可制度

senses.title: Permission granted by an authority
senses.titleCN: 官方许可：权威解除禁令
senses.definition: official permission from a government or other authority to do something that is otherwise controlled or forbidden
senses.definitionCN: 政府或其他权威机构给予的正式许可，使原本受管制或被禁止的事可以做
senses.example: The company applied for a license to drill in the bay.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司申请在海湾钻探的许可证。
senses.why: The Latin source is licere 'to be allowed', and its noun licentia meant 'freedom, permission'. The core scene is not a piece of paper but a gatekeeper lifting a ban, so the first sense is the permission itself; it can even be uncountable, as in work under license.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源头是 licere“被允许”，其名词 licentia 意为“自由、许可”。核心画面不是一张纸，而是守门人解除禁令，所以第一义项是许可本身；它甚至可作不可数用法，如 work under license（经许可工作）。

senses.title: The document that carries the permission
senses.titleCN: 执照：把许可变成可携带的证件
senses.definition: an official card, certificate, or document that shows the holder has been given permission to do something
senses.definitionCN: 表明持有人已获准做某事的官方卡片、证书或文件
senses.example: He handed his driver's license to the officer at the checkpoint.
senses.exampleCN: 他在检查站把驾照递给了警官。
senses.why: Permission needs proof once it leaves the office. By metonymy the abstract grant becomes the object in your pocket: a driver's license, a business license, a hunting license. This is the countable, everyday sense and the one that takes a plural.
senses.whyCN: 许可一旦离开办公室就需要凭证。借代让抽象的授予变成口袋里的实物：驾照、营业执照、狩猎证。这是可数、最日常的义项，也是能变复数的那个。

senses.title: A contract granting rights to use a work
senses.titleCN: 授权协议：允许他人使用作品或权利
senses.definition: a legal agreement under which the owner of a copyright, patent, or trademark allows another party to use it, usually for a fee
senses.definitionCN: 版权、专利或商标所有人允许另一方使用其权利的法律协议，通常收取费用
senses.example: The publisher bought a license to translate the novel into Chinese.
senses.exampleCN: 出版社买下了把这部小说译成中文的授权。
senses.why: Here licentia is narrowed from general permission to one specified right. The owner keeps ownership and hands over only a limited freedom, which is why a license is signed rather than sold: the thing granted is use, not title.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 licentia 从笼统许可收窄为一项特定权利。所有人保留所有权，只交出一部分有限自由，所以 license 是“签授权”而不是“卖断”：授予的是使用权，不是所有权。

senses.title: Literary liberty: freedom without restraint
senses.titleCN: 放纵的自由：不受约束的状态（古义/文学）
senses.definition: freedom to act as one pleases, especially when it goes beyond accepted limits; an older literary sense of the word
senses.definitionCN: 想怎么做就怎么做的自由，尤指超出公认界限；该词较古老的文学义
senses.example: During the carnival, a spirit of license swept through the streets.
senses.exampleCN: 狂欢节期间，一种放纵的自由气息席卷街头。
senses.why: Latin licentia could mean both 'permission' and 'unrestrained freedom'. English kept the second branch: a license can be a state of liberty, not a document. Modern British usage usually spells this noun licence, while the verb remains license.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 licentia 既可指“许可”，也可指“不受约束的自由”。英语保留了第二条分支：license 可以是自由状态而非文件。现代英式英语中该名词通常拼作 licence，动词仍作 license。

senses.title: To authorize an activity officially
senses.titleCN: 正式批准：官方放行某项活动
senses.definition: to give official permission for an activity, or to issue a permit to a person or business
senses.definitionCN: 正式批准某项活动，或向个人、企业发放许可证
senses.example: Only the city can license a new restaurant kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 只有市政府才能给新的餐馆厨房发许可证。
senses.why: The verb is recorded from about 1400 and was formed directly from the noun. The authority is the subject, the permitted activity is the object, and the act is a formal yes rather than a description of freedom.
senses.whyCN: 动词约在 1400 年出现，直接由名词转化而来。主语是权威机构，宾语是被批准的活动，这个动作是一个正式的“可以”，而不是对自由状态的描述。

senses.title: To grant the right to use intellectual property
senses.titleCN: 授权使用：把知识产权许可出去
senses.definition: to give a person or company legal permission to use a copyrighted work, invention, or brand
senses.definitionCN: 给予个人或公司使用受版权保护的作品、发明或品牌的法律许可
senses.example: The studio licensed the character for a series of toys.
senses.exampleCN: 工作室把这个角色的使用权授权给了一系列玩具。
senses.why: This is sense 3 as a verb. The owner stays the owner and lets someone else exploit the right; the object is a work or a right, not an activity, which separates it from license a restaurant in sense 5.
senses.whyCN: 这是第 3 义项的动词化。所有人仍是所有人，只允许别人利用这项权利；宾语是作品或权利，而不是活动，因此区别于第 5 义项的“给餐馆发证”。

senses.title: Social permission: a reason to speak or act
senses.titleCN: 理据性许可：有理由开口或行动
senses.definition: a fact, status, or circumstance that gives someone the freedom or justification to do something
senses.definitionCN: 某种事实、身份或情境给予某人做某事的自由或正当理由
senses.example: Twenty years of service gave her license to question the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 二十年的服务经历给了她质疑这项计划的底气。
senses.why: No office is involved. The authority is experience, rank, or custom, and the phrase a license to do something treats that social standing as a grant. The word still performs the same act: it removes the risk of being thought out of line.
senses.whyCN: 这里没有发证机关。权威是经验、地位或惯例，而 a license to do something 这一说法把社会身份当成一种授予。这个词仍在做同一件事：消除“越界”的顾虑。

senses.title: Artistic license: the right to break the rules
senses.titleCN: 艺术破格：为效果而偏离事实或规则
senses.definition: the freedom that artists, writers, or performers claim to change facts, rules, or language in order to achieve an effect
senses.definitionCN: 艺术家、作家或表演者为达到效果而改变事实、规则或语言时自称的自由
senses.example: The film takes poetic license with the historical record.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影对历史记载做了诗意的破格处理。
senses.why: The fixed phrase poetic license shows the word at its most permissive: the permission comes from convention rather than an office, and the deviation is expected to serve the work rather than deceive the audience.
senses.whyCN: 固定短语 poetic license 展示了这个词最宽松的一面：许可来自惯例而不是机关，而这种偏离被期待是服务于作品，而不是欺骗观众。

senses.title: Fixed compounds and the licence/license spelling line
senses.titleCN: 固定搭配与拼写边界：license plate、licence/license
senses.definition: the noun as it survives in fixed compounds such as license plate, and the British and American rules that separate the noun licence from the verb license
senses.definitionCN: 名词在 license plate 等固定搭配中的用法，以及英式、美式把名词 licence 与动词 license 分开的拼写规则
senses.example: In British English the noun is licence and the verb is license; American English uses license for both.
senses.exampleCN: 英式英语中名词是 licence、动词是 license；美式英语两者都用 license。
senses.why: Compounds freeze the noun, which is why American license plate keeps the s. The spelling split follows the French-derived noun and the later English verb, standardized differently in Britain and America in the 18th and 19th centuries; in Britain the c marks the noun, the s marks the verb.
senses.whyCN: 复合词把名词形式固定下来，所以美式 license plate 保留 s。拼写分裂则源于法语来源的名词与后来英语派生的动词，18—19 世纪在英美分别被标准化成不同规则；英式用 c 标记名词、用 s 标记动词。

intro.en: License is a permission word, not a law word. Latin licere 'to be allowed, to be lawful' produced licentia 'freedom, permission', which Old French passed to English as licence. The modern split between the noun and the verb, and between British and American spelling, came much later.
intro.cn: license 是“许可”词，不是“法律”词。拉丁语 licere“被允许、合法”产生名词 licentia“自由、许可”，古法语把 licence 传给英语。名词与动词的分工、以及英美拼写的差异，都是后来才形成的。

items.en: Latin licere 'to be allowed, to be lawful' gave the noun licentia 'freedom, permission, license' and the participle licitus 'allowed'. The core idea is permission granted, not a statute enacted.
items.cn: 拉丁语 licere“被允许、合法”产生了名词 licentia“自由、许可、执照”和分词 licitus“获准的”。核心观念是“被授予许可”，而不是“制定法律”。

items.en: The deeper origin is uncertain. Licere is generally thought to go back to a PIE root *leik- 'to offer, bargain', also seen in Latin liceri 'to bid at auction'; this is a reconstruction, not a documented fact, and the intermediate steps are not certain.
items.cn: 更深的来源不确定。一般认为 licere 可追溯到原始印欧语词根 *leik-“出价、议价”，也见于拉丁语 liceri“拍卖出价”；这属于构拟，不是有文献确证的事实，中间环节并不确定。

items.en: Old French licence (12c.–13c.) meant 'freedom, liberty, permission' and came from Latin licentia. English borrowed the word rather than building it from parts.
items.cn: 古法语 licence（12—13 世纪）意为“自由、自主、许可”，来自拉丁语 licentia。英语是整词借入，而不是自己用词素拼出来的。

items.en: The noun is recorded in English in the late 14c. with both 'liberty, freedom' and 'formal permission from a superior'. The verb appears about 1400 as 'to give formal authority', and a 'give free rein' sense is recorded in the 1530s.
items.cn: 名词在 14 世纪晚期的英语中已有记录，兼有“自由、自主”和“上级的正式许可”两义。动词约 1400 年出现，意为“授予正式权限”；“放任、放开”义见于 16 世纪 30 年代。

items.en: The freedom branch stayed strong in the 16c.–17c., when licentious 'morally unrestrained' entered English from licentiosus. The permit branch gradually became the dominant everyday meaning, leaving the freedom branch as literary and archaic.
items.cn: “自由、放纵”这一支在 16—17 世纪仍很活跃，licentious“道德上无节制”就是此时从 licentiosus 进入英语的。此后“许可证”这一支逐渐成为日常主义，“自由”义退居文学与古旧用法。

items.en: License is not from Latin lex 'law' (genitive legis), which belongs to a different root and gives legal and legislate; the two words talk about rules but are not related. British English keeps licence for the noun and license for the verb; American English uses license for both. Compounds such as license plate, license fee and license holder keep the noun form.
items.cn: license 并非出自拉丁语 lex“法律”（属格 legis）；lex 属于另一个词根，衍生出 legal、legislate。两个词都谈规则，却不同源。英式英语名词用 licence、动词用 license；美式英语两者都用 license。license plate、license fee、license holder 等复合词则固定保留名词形式。

note.en: The look-alikes either belong to the Latin licere family or mark the noun/verb spelling line; the near synonyms each grant permission from a different angle.
note.cn: 第一组要么属于拉丁语 licere 词族，要么标记名词与动词的拼写分界；第二组则从不同角度表达“准许”。

entries.definition: The British spelling of the noun only. British usage keeps licence for the permission or the document and license for the verb; American usage uses license for both.
entries.definitionCN: 只用于英式名词的拼写。英式用法中，表示许可或许可证的名词作 licence，动词作 license；美式则两者都用 license。

entries.definition: Lawful or permitted, from Latin licitus, the participle of licere. It is an adjective, not a permit, and has no verb use.
entries.definitionCN: 合法的、获准的，来自拉丁语 licitus（licere 的分词）。它是形容词，不指证件，也没有动词用法。

entries.definition: Morally unrestrained, especially in sexual matters, from licentia 'freedom' plus -osus 'full of'. It carries only the excessive-liberty branch, never the permit branch.
entries.definitionCN: 道德上无节制的，尤指性方面，来自 licentia“自由”加 -osus“充满……的”。它只继承“过度自由”这一支，从不表示许可证。

entries.definition: To allow something, or an official document that allows it. It is the closest everyday synonym, though a permit is often a specific written allowance such as a parking permit, while a license usually certifies a professional or legal right.
entries.definitionCN: 允许某事，或允许做某事的官方文件。它是最接近的日常同义词；但 permit 多指具体的书面允许（如停车证），而 license 常指对专业资格或法律权利的认证。

entries.definition: The act of allowing or the state of being allowed. It names the abstract grant only, never the card in your pocket, and it has no verb sense of issuing a license.
entries.definitionCN: 允许的行为或被允许的状态。它只指抽象的授予，不指口袋里的证件，也没有“发许可证”的动词义。

entries.definition: Official power or approval to act. It stresses the authority behind the grant rather than the paper or the freedom that follows.
entries.definitionCN: 做某事的官方权力或批准。它强调授予背后的权威，而不是证件本身或随之而来的自由。

entries.definition: A right granted by a company or government to sell goods or run a service under its name. It is a kind of license, but tied to a brand or a monopoly rather than to a single activity.
entries.definitionCN: 公司或政府授予的、以其名义销售商品或经营服务的权利。它是许可的一种，但绑定品牌或垄断经营权，而不是单项活动。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin licere 'to be allowed' plus -entia, with licit, illicit, licentious and leisure in the same Latin family.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词与真实同族词：拉丁语 licere“被允许”加 -entia，licit、illicit、licentious、leisure 都在同一个拉丁词族里。

normal.en: licere means 'to be allowed'. License is the allowed-ness itself, before it is ever a card in a wallet.
normal.cn: licere 意为“被允许”。license 首先就是这种“获准状态”，然后才变成钱包里的卡片。

normal.en: licentia covered both 'permission' and 'freedom'. The modern word still keeps the old freedom branch in literary use, as in a spirit of license.
normal.cn: licentia 兼有“许可”与“自由”两义。现代英语仍在文学语境里保留“自由”这一支，如 a spirit of license（放纵的气息）。

normal.en: The paper sense is a metonymy: the grant stands for the document that proves it, so a driver's license is both permission and proof.
normal.cn: 证件义是借代：授予本身代替了证明它的文件，所以 driver's license 既是许可也是凭证。

normal.en: Do not connect license to lex 'law'. Lex is about statutes and gives legal and legislate; licere is about being permitted, and the two only happen to talk about rules.
normal.cn: 不要把 license 连到 lex“法律”。lex 指成文法规，衍生出 legal、legislate；licere 指“被允许”，两者只是碰巧都谈规则。

normal.en: Spelling: British noun licence, British verb license; American both license. The c/s line marks word class, not a difference in meaning.
normal.cn: 拼写：英式名词 licence、动词 license；美式两者都写 license。c 与 s 这条线标记的是词性，不是意义差别。

abstract.en: Picture a locked door with a guard. License is the guard stepping aside — the permission itself, not the door and not the key.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇锁着的门和一名守卫。license 是守卫让开的那一下——是许可本身，不是门，也不是钥匙。

abstract.en: Then the guard hands you a card so that other guards will step aside too. That card is the second sense, the license you carry.
abstract.cn: 然后守卫递给你一张卡，好让别的守卫也让开。那张卡就是第 2 义项，你随身携带的许可证。

abstract.en: When there is no guard at all, license becomes the freedom to act, which is why poets claim poetic license to break the rules on purpose.
abstract.cn: 当根本没有守卫时，license 就变成行动的自由；诗人正是据此主张 poetic license，故意打破规则。

examples.en: The university licenses its software to students at a reduced fee.
examples.cn: 这所大学以优惠价格把软件授权给学生使用。

examples.en: Her position gave her license to challenge the chair.
examples.cn: 她的职位给了她质疑主席的底气。

examples.en: In British English, licence is the noun and license is the verb.
examples.cn: 在英式英语中，licence 是名词，license 是动词。

dict_mnemonic.text: “来sense”——官方来了这份许可，事情才 sense 得通 → license 许可证；许可

root: 拉丁语 licere“被允许、合法”→ 名词 licentia“许可、自由”。核心是“权威解除禁令、放行”，再由“许可”引申出证件、授权协议、自由放纵与艺术破格；与 lex“法律”并非同源。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of license, one movement: an authority lifts a ban, the permission becomes a document, then a limited right, then a social justification, and finally a freedom that needs no office at all.
sensesIntro.cn: license 的九个义项是一条线：权威解除禁令，许可变成证件，再收窄为有限权利，又转成社会层面的底气，最后成为无需发证机关的自由。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an authority hands over a key, and a door that was locked can now be opened.
core.cn: 核心意象：权威递出一把钥匙，原本锁着的门现在可以被推开。

branches.en: AUTHORITY: an authority lifts a ban, and the verb is that lifting done officially and out loud.
branches.cn: 权威：权威解除禁令，动词就是这一解除被正式、公开地做出。

branches.en: PAPER: permission becomes a document you carry, and compounds plus spelling freeze its noun form.
branches.cn: 纸面：许可变成随身携带的证件，而复合词与拼写规则又把名词形式固定下来。

branches.en: RIGHTS: a limited right is granted while ownership stays with the owner, in both the noun and the verb.
branches.cn: 权利：只授予有限使用权，所有权仍留给所有人；名词与动词都走这一支。

branches.en: FREEDOM: from unrestrained liberty to the artist's licensed deviation from fact and rule.
branches.cn: 自由：从不受约束的放纵，到艺术家获准偏离事实与规则。

branches.en: JUSTIFICATION: status, experience or custom acts as the authority that grants the permission.
branches.cn: 理据：地位、经验或惯例充当授予许可的“权威”。

intro.en: License is a borrowed Latin noun, not an English prefix-plus-root construction. English adds only ordinary suffixes such as -ed, -ee, -or and -ure; the endings -nce and -nse belong to the borrowed word itself.
intro.cn: license 是借入的拉丁名词，不是英语“前缀＋词根”的构造。英语只加 -ed、-ee、-or、-ure 这类普通后缀；-nce 与 -nse 的词尾属于借词本身。

latinIntro.en: Inside Latin, licere produced licentia and licitus, and those yielded English licence/license, licit, illicit and licentious. Leisure reaches English through Old French and is generally traced to the same licere.
latinIntro.cn: 在拉丁语内部，licere 产生了 licentia 与 licitus，后者衍生出英语的 licence/license、licit、illicit、licentious。leisure 经古法语进入英语，一般也追溯到同一个 licere。

items.structure: license + -ed (past participle used as an adjective)
items.meaning: having official permission to do something
items.meaningCN: 已获官方许可的；持证的（-ed 构成形容词）
items.example: Only licensed drivers may use this road.
items.exampleCN: 只有持证司机才能使用这条路。

items.meaning: a person or company that has been given a license
items.meaningCN: 被许可人；持证人（-ee 表示接受者）
items.example: The licensee must renew the permit every year.
items.exampleCN: 被许可人必须每年续办许可证。

items.meaning: the party that grants a license to another party
items.meaningCN: 许可人；授权方（-or 表示施动者）
items.example: The licensor keeps ownership of the trademark.
items.exampleCN: 许可人保留该商标的所有权。

items.meaning: the act or system of granting licenses, especially for a profession
items.meaningCN: 许可的颁发；执业许可制度（-ure 构成行为或状态名词）
items.example: Nursing licensure requires a state examination.
items.exampleCN: 护士执业许可需要参加州级考试。

items.meaning: to be allowed, to be permitted
items.example: The verb is the permission behind every sense of license.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是 license 各义项背后的“许可”。

items.meaning: permission; unrestrained freedom
items.example: Latin licentia already carried both permission and excess.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 licentia 已同时带有“许可”与“放纵”。

items.meaning: permitted, lawful
items.example: Its opposite illicit marks what the law forbids.
items.exampleCN: 它的反义词 illicit 标出法律禁止之事。

items.meaning: an act or its result
items.example: It forms licensure, the granting of licences.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 licensure，即执照的颁发。

items.meaning: without a licence
items.example: The city fined the unlicensed vendor.
items.exampleCN: 市政对那个无照摊贩开了罚单。

latinEntries.meaning: lawful or permitted
latinEntries.meaningCN: 合法的；获准的（与 license 同源，保留拉丁分词义）

latinEntries.meaning: not allowed by law or custom
latinEntries.meaningCN: 非法的；违禁的；不正当的

latinEntries.meaning: morally unrestrained, especially in sexual matters
latinEntries.meaningCN: 放荡的；无节制的（只继承“过度自由”义）

latinEntries.structure: Old French leisir, generally traced to Latin licere (to be allowed)
latinEntries.meaning: free time, time at one's disposal
latinEntries.meaningCN: 闲暇；空闲时间（本义一般认为是“被允许自由支配的时间”）

definition_zh: 同样地；也；此外；彼此彼此
definition_en: in the same way; also; used to add a parallel statement or to return a wish or greeting
core_image: 两枚形状相同的印章，在同一张纸上压出同样的印痕
scene: 设计评审会上，第一组把图标改成圆角。The second team did likewise, keeping the same corner radius and the same grid spacing as the first.
sceneCN: 这里 likewise 是「以同样的方式」（第 1 个义项：方式相同）；句意：第二组也照样做，沿用和第一组一样的圆角与网格间距。图中可辨识物件：两组并排的界面草图、同一套圆角网格、配色卡。

pos.zh: 同样地；也；此外；同样（用于回应）

collocations.zh: 同样地，……（句首引出平行论断）
以及诸如此类；同样还有
以同样的方式对待某人
回一句“彼此彼此／我也是”

senses.title: Same manner: in the same way
senses.titleCN: 同样方式：照着同一套做法
senses.definition: in the same way or by the same method as someone or something else
senses.definitionCN: 以与别人或别的事物相同的方式或方法
senses.example: She folded the map carefully, and he did likewise.
senses.exampleCN: 她仔细折好地图，他也照样做了。
senses.why: The word joins like, 'having the same form', to wise, 'manner'. The first sense is therefore the plain arithmetic of the compound: same form plus manner equals same way of doing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把表示“具有相同形体”的 like 与表示“方式”的 wise 合在一起。因此第一个义项就是这层构词关系的直接结果：相同形体加方式，等于相同的做法。

senses.title: Addition: the same is true of the second item
senses.titleCN: 追加：第二项也如此
senses.definition: also or too, used when a second person or thing shares the same action, quality, or situation
senses.definitionCN: 也、同样，用于第二个人或物享有同一动作、性质或处境时
senses.example: The first proposal was too costly; the second was likewise rejected.
senses.exampleCN: 第一份提案成本太高；第二份也同样被否决了。
senses.why: Repeating an action in the same way easily becomes repeating the same verdict. The adverb slides from describing how something is done to asserting that the same predicate applies again.
senses.whyCN: 用同样的方式重复一个动作，很容易变成重复同一个结论。这个词于是从描述“怎么做”，滑向断定“同样的说法对第二项也成立”。

senses.title: Parallel clause marker: a matching statement follows
senses.titleCN: 平行句标记：引出结构对应的下一句
senses.definition: at the start of a sentence, used to introduce a statement that runs parallel to the previous one
senses.definitionCN: 置于句首，引出与上一句结构或逻辑平行的陈述
senses.example: The north wing needs repair. Likewise, the roof must be replaced.
senses.exampleCN: 北翼需要修缮。同样地，屋顶也必须更换。
senses.why: Once the adverb sits at the head of a clause, it stops modifying a single verb and starts organizing discourse: the next clause is offered as a second panel of the same picture.
senses.whyCN: 当这个副词移到从句开头，它就不再修饰单个动词，而开始组织语篇：下一句被当作同一幅图的第二块面板呈现出来。

senses.title: Reciprocal reply: the same to you
senses.titleCN: 回应套语：彼此彼此
senses.definition: in conversation, a short reply meaning 'the same to you' or 'I feel the same'
senses.definitionCN: 口语中简短回应，意为“你也一样”或“我也有同感”
senses.example: "Have a good trip." "Likewise."
senses.exampleCN: “旅途愉快。”“彼此彼此。”
senses.why: The comparison turns back on the speaker: the wish or feeling just received is returned to the sender. A whole clause is compressed into one adverb.
senses.whyCN: 比较的方向转回说话者：刚收到的祝愿或感受被原样送还给对方。整个从句被压缩成一个副词。

senses.title: Correspondence: standing in the same relation
