forms.label: 复数／三单（名词复数、动词三单，同形）

senses.title: The heavier side of a comparison: more important
senses.titleCN: 比较中更重的一侧：更重要
senses.definition: more important, more powerful, or more effective than other things of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 在同类别中更重要、更有力量或更有效
senses.example: Tourism is a major source of income for the island.
senses.exampleCN: 旅游业是这个岛的主要收入来源。
senses.why: Latin maior is the comparative of magnus 'great'. The word begins as a weighing: two things are compared and one side is heavier. Importance is the first thing this comparison measures, before size or number.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 maior 是 magnus“大”的比较级。这个词的起点是一次称量：两样东西相比，有一侧更重。这个比较最先量的是重要性，然后才是尺寸或数量。

senses.title: Greater in scale or quantity
senses.titleCN: 规模或数量更大
senses.definition: larger in size, number, or extent when measured against others
senses.definitionCN: 与其他事物相比，在尺寸、数量或范围上更大
senses.example: A major portion of the budget goes to salaries.
senses.exampleCN: 预算的一大部分用于工资。
senses.why: The same scale now reads quantity rather than rank. Because maior already carries 'more', careful English does not say 'very major': a big city can be a major city, but major itself never means merely big.
senses.whyCN: 同一架天平现在量的是数量而不是位次。由于 maior 本身已含“更多”，规范的英语不说 very major：大城市可以是 major city，但 major 本身从不只表示“尺寸大”。

senses.title: Serious enough to matter: medical and risk use
senses.titleCN: 重大到需要重视：医疗与风险用法
senses.definition: serious in effect or risk, especially of surgery, illness, damage, or change
senses.definitionCN: 在后果或风险上严重，尤用于手术、疾病、损害或变化
senses.example: The patient needs major surgery on his knee.
senses.exampleCN: 这位病人需要接受膝关节大手术。
senses.why: In medicine the comparison is between procedures that threaten the body and those that do not. A major operation is not simply bigger; it carries a higher risk, so the comparative becomes a judgement of severity.
senses.whyCN: 在医学里，比较的两端是威胁身体的手术与不威胁身体的手术。大手术不只是“更大”，而是风险更高，因此比较级变成了一种严重程度的判断。

senses.title: Music: the scale a half-step greater
senses.titleCN: 音乐：高出半音的音阶
senses.definition: of a scale, key, or chord built on a major third, sounding brighter and more stable than the minor
senses.definitionCN: 指以大三级为基础的音阶、调或和弦，听感比小调明亮、稳定
senses.example: The piece moves from a minor key into a bright major key.
senses.exampleCN: 这首曲子从小调转入明亮的大调。
senses.why: Music borrowed the word in the 1690s because a major interval is a half-step 'greater' than the minor one. The comparison is now measured on the keyboard rather than on a scale of importance.
senses.whyCN: 音乐在 17 世纪 90 年代借用这个词，因为大三度比小三度“多”一个半音。此时比较是在键盘上量的，而不是在重要性的尺度上量的。

senses.title: University: the subject weighted most
senses.titleCN: 大学：分量最重的学科
senses.definition: the main subject a student specializes in, or to specialize in that subject
senses.definitionCN: 学生专攻的主修科目，或专攻该科目
senses.example: She majored in economics and minored in statistics.
senses.exampleCN: 她主修经济学，辅修统计学。
senses.why: A degree is a set of subjects, and one of them is weighted more heavily than the rest. The noun 'subject of specialization' is recorded by 1890 and the verb by 1910, both keeping the heavier side of the balance.
senses.whyCN: 一个学位由若干科目组成，其中一门的分量重于其余。名词义“专业”记录于 1890 年，动词义记录于 1910 年，两者都保留了天平上更重的那一侧。

senses.title: Military rank: the senior officer
senses.titleCN: 军衔：资历更高的军官
senses.definition: an officer rank above captain and below lieutenant colonel
senses.definitionCN: 高于上尉、低于中校的军官军衔
senses.example: The major briefed the company commanders before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 少校在黎明前向各连长做了简报。
senses.why: The rank came through French major, short for sergent-major, from Medieval Latin major 'chief officer'. In a body of officers one is marked as the senior one, so the comparative is used as a title.
senses.whyCN: 这个军衔经法语 major（sergent-major 的缩略）来自中世纪拉丁语 major“首席军官”。在一群军官中有一人被标为资历更高者，于是比较级被用作头衔。

senses.title: Legal adulthood: the older side of the line
senses.titleCN: 法定成年：年龄界线另一侧的人
senses.definition: a person who has reached the age of legal adulthood, or the state of being of full legal age
senses.definitionCN: 已达到法定成年年龄的人，或处于完全法定成年状态
senses.example: A minor cannot sign the contract; a major can.
senses.exampleCN: 未成年人不能签这份合同，成年人可以。
senses.why: Medieval Latin major also named 'an elder, an adult'. Law needs a line between those who can bind themselves and those who cannot, and major marks the person on the older side of that line.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪拉丁语 major 也指“年长者、成年人”。法律需要在能为自己负责与不能负责的人之间划一条线，major 标记的就是这条线年长一侧的人。

senses.title: The top tier: major leagues and the majors
senses.titleCN: 最高层级：大联盟与顶级行列
senses.definition: in sport and business, the highest level of competition or the largest organizations, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 在体育与商业中，最高级别的赛事或最大的机构，常用复数
senses.example: He spent six seasons in the majors before returning to coach.
senses.exampleCN: 他在顶级联赛打了六个赛季，之后回去当教练。
senses.why: Major league is recorded in baseball by 1892. The comparison now runs between leagues rather than people: one circuit is the greater one, and 'the majors' became shorthand for the top tier in any field.
senses.whyCN: major league 在棒球中记录于 1892 年。此时比较发生在联盟之间而不是人之间：有一个联盟是“更大”的，于是 the majors 成了任何领域顶级行列的简称。

senses.title: Usage boundary: major is not simply big
senses.titleCN: 用法边界：major 不等于“尺寸大”
senses.definition: major describes importance or seriousness rather than physical size alone; it is not graded with very, and minor is its usual opposite
senses.definitionCN: major 描述重要性或严重性，而不只是物理尺寸；它不用 very 分级，其通常的反义词是 minor
senses.example: The storm caused major delays, though the airport itself is not very big.
senses.exampleCN: 这场风暴造成了严重延误，尽管机场本身并不大。
senses.why: Because maior is already a comparative, 'very major' is redundant in careful use. A major city is important, not necessarily large; a big city is large, not necessarily important. Major and minor split one scale into two sides.
senses.whyCN: 由于 maior 已是比较级，规范的用法中 very major 是冗余的。major city 是重要的城市，不一定面积大；big city 是面积大的城市，不一定重要。major 与 minor 把同一把尺子分成两侧。

intro.en: Major is the comparative form of the Latin word for 'great'. It entered English around 1300 as a word of rank, and later spread to quantity, music, universities, armies and leagues — always marking the heavier side of a comparison.
intro.cn: major 是拉丁语“大”的比较级形式。它约在 1300 年进入英语，最初表示位次高低，后来扩展到数量、音乐、大学、军队和联赛——始终标记比较中更重的一侧。

items.en: First recorded in English as majour, 'greater, more important or effective, leading, principal'. From c. 1300 it also named an elder or an adult.
items.cn: 最早以 majour 记录于英语，意为“更大的、更重要的或更有效的、领先的、主要的”。约 1300 年起也指年长者或成年人。

items.en: From Latin maior (earlier *magios), the irregular comparative of magnus 'large, great'. A comparative built on a suppletive stem, not on a regular -ior suffix added to magnus.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 maior（更早作 *magios），是 magnus“大”的不规则比较级。它是建立在异干互补词干上的比较级，并不是在 magnus 后加规则的 -ior。

items.en: magnus and maior are traced to PIE *meg- 'great', the same root behind magnify, magnitude and master. This reconstruction is generally accepted rather than proven.
items.cn: magnus 与 maior 被追溯到原始印欧语 *meg-“大”，也是 magnify、magnitude、master 的词根。这一重构属于一般认为，而非确证。

items.en: The sense 'greater in quantity, number, or extent' is recorded from the 1590s, extending the comparison from rank to measurable scale.
items.cn: “数量、数目或范围更大”的义项记录于 16 世纪 90 年代，把比较从位次扩展到可测量的规模。

items.en: The military rank appears in the 1640s via French major, short for sergent-major. The musical sense follows in the 1690s, from the idea of an interval a half-step 'greater' than the minor.
items.cn: 军衔义在 17 世纪 40 年代经法语 major（sergent-major 的缩略）出现。音乐义随后在 17 世纪 90 年代出现，来自“比小调音程多半音”的观念。

items.en: The academic noun 'subject of specialization' is recorded by 1890, major league by 1892, and the verb 'to focus one's studies' by 1910 in American English.
items.cn: 学术名词义“专业”记录于 1890 年，major league 记录于 1892 年，动词义“专注学业”记录于 1910 年，属美式英语。

note.en: The first group shares the maior / magnus line or looks close to it. The second group separates words for rank, importance, size and degree, which English often uses interchangeably and often should not.
note.cn: 第一组共享 maior／magnus 这条线，或词形接近。第二组区分位次、重要性、尺寸与程度——英语常把它们混用，而很多时候不该混用。

entries.definition: the larger number or part; also the age of legal adulthood. It is the noun built on maior, not a synonym of major.
entries.definitionCN: 多数、较大部分；也指法定成年年龄。它是建立在 maior 上的名词，不是 major 的同义词。

entries.definition: the elected head of a city. It came through French maire from Latin maior 'greater, chief', so it is a cousin, not a derivative of English major.
entries.definitionCN: 民选市长。它经法语 maire 来自拉丁语 maior“更大、首领”，因此是远亲，而不是英语 major 的派生词。

entries.definition: grand and impressive in appearance. It comes from majesty, from Latin maiestas, built on the same maior 'greater' stem.
entries.definitionCN: 外观宏伟、威严的。它来自 majesty，再上溯拉丁语 maiestas，同样建立在 maior“更大”的词干上。

entries.definition: largest or most important among several. It is close to major but usually points to one clear leader, as in the main reason.
entries.definitionCN: 在若干者中最大或最重要的。它接近 major，但通常指向一个明确的领头者，如 the main reason。

entries.definition: highest in rank or authority. It stresses position at the top of a hierarchy, while major stresses weight in a comparison.
entries.definitionCN: 位次或权力最高的。它强调层级顶端的位置，而 major 强调比较中的分量。

entries.definition: first in importance, especially of a reason, aim, or sum. It is more formal and narrower than major.
entries.definitionCN: 最重要的，尤用于理由、目标或款项。它比 major 更正式，适用范围更窄。

entries.definition: large or important enough to be noticed or to matter. It can measure degree where major measures rank.
entries.definitionCN: 大到或重要到值得注意、值得当回事。它可量程度，而 major 量位次。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: maior is the comparative of magnus, and the same 'great' stem runs through majority, majesty, magnify, magnitude and master.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词与真实同族词：maior 是 magnus 的比较级，同一条“大”词干贯穿 majority、majesty、magnify、magnitude、master。

normal.en: maior is a comparative, so major always implies 'than the other one'. A major road matters more than a minor road, not because it is wider.
normal.cn: maior 是比较级，所以 major 总隐含“比另一个更……”。主干道比次要道路重要，不是因为它更宽。

normal.en: magnus 'great' gives magnify, magnitude and magnate; maior gives major, majority and majesty. One family, two stems.
normal.cn: magnus“大”给出 magnify、magnitude、magnate；maior 给出 major、majority、majesty。同一个家族，两条词干。

normal.en: The academic major is the subject given the most weight in a degree, which is why the same word also means 'the important one'.
normal.cn: 大学的 major 是学位中分量最重的科目，这也是同一个词又表示“重要的那一个”的原因。

normal.en: A major in the army is the senior officer in a group, and a legal major is the older person across the age line: both are the 'greater' side.
normal.cn: 军队里的 major 是一群军官中资历更高者，法律上的 major 是年龄界线另一侧的年长者：两者都是“更大”的那一侧。

normal.en: Major league and the majors keep the comparison between leagues: the top circuit is the greater one.
normal.cn: major league 与 the majors 保留的是联盟之间的比较：顶级联盟就是“更大”的那一个。

abstract.en: Picture a balance with two pans. Whatever is placed in them, major names the pan that sinks: more weight, more rank, more risk, more volume.
abstract.cn: 想象一架两端有托盘的天平。无论放进去的是什么，major 指的都是下沉的那一盘：更多分量、更高位次、更大风险、更大体量。

abstract.en: The comparison can be held between cities, keys, subjects, officers or leagues; only the scale changes, never the gesture of weighing.
abstract.cn: 比较可以发生在城市、调式、学科、军官或联盟之间；变的只是尺子，称量这个动作从未改变。

abstract.en: Because one pan is already lower, there is no room to add 'very': the comparison is complete before the adjective is spoken.
abstract.cn: 因为有一盘已经更低，“very”就无处可加：比较在形容词出口之前就已经完成了。

examples.en: Lack of sleep was a major factor in the accident.
examples.cn: 睡眠不足是这起事故的一个主要因素。

examples.en: She majored in history and later became a curator.
examples.cn: 她主修历史，后来成了策展人。

examples.en: The symphony ends in a confident major key.
examples.cn: 这首交响曲在一个自信的大调上结束。

dict_mnemonic.text: “梅杰”——梅杰先生主修经济学，后来升为少校 → major 主要的、主修、少校

root: 拉丁语 maior“更大的”，是 magnus“大”的比较级，核心是“两者相比更重、更高的一侧”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of major, all one act of weighing: importance, scale, severity, a musical interval, a chosen subject, an officer's rank, legal age, the top league, and the boundary where the word stops meaning 'big'.
sensesIntro.cn: major 的九个义项都出自同一次称量：重要性、规模、严重程度、音程、主修科目、军衔、法定成年、顶级联盟，以及它不再表示“尺寸大”的用法边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two things are weighed, and major names the heavier pan.
core.cn: 核心意象：两样东西被称量，major 指更重的那一盘。

branches.en: WEIGHT: importance and quantity are the same comparison read on two different scales.
branches.cn: 分量：重要性与数量是同一场比较在两把不同尺子上的读数。

branches.en: SEVERITY: in medicine the heavier side is the higher risk, so the comparison becomes a warning.
branches.cn: 严重性：在医学里更重的一侧就是更高风险，于是比较变成一种警示。

branches.en: INTERVAL: music measures the greater interval on the keyboard, a half-step above the minor.
branches.cn: 音程：音乐在键盘上量出更大的音程，比小调高一个半音。

branches.en: SELECTION: a chosen subject and a top league are both the item given the most weight in a set.
branches.cn: 选择：主修科目与顶级联盟都是在集合中被赋予最大分量的那一项。

branches.en: RANK, AGE AND BOUNDARY: a senior officer and an adult past the legal line are the greater side of a hierarchy, while the last branch marks the point where major stops meaning 'big'.
branches.cn: 位次、年龄与边界：资历更高的军官与越过法定年龄线的成年人是层级中更大的一侧；最后一条标出 major 不再表示“尺寸大”的分界。

intro.en: Major is not built with a living English prefix. Its Latin stem maior is already a comparative; English only adds noun and adverb suffixes to the finished word.
intro.cn: major 不是用活的英语前缀构成的。它的拉丁词干 maior 本身已是比较级；英语只是在成品词后加名词与副词后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family splits into two stems: magnus 'great' (magnify, magnitude) and its comparative maior 'greater' (major, majority, majesty). They are one root seen from two angles.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族分成两条词干：magnus“大”（magnify、magnitude）及其比较级 maior“更大”（major、majority、majesty）。它们是同一个词根的两个视角。

items.structure: Medieval Latin majoritas, from maior (greater) + -itas (noun of state)
items.meaning: the larger part of a group; the winning number of votes; the age of legal adulthood
items.meaningCN: 多数；多数票；法定成年（-ity 构成状态或性质名词）
items.example: The majority of members voted for the change.
items.exampleCN: 多数成员投票支持这项改变。

items.meaning: extremely, or in a major way (informal)
items.example: I am majorly late for the meeting.
items.exampleCN: 我开会要迟到大发了。

items.meaning: a military officer ranked below a lieutenant general
items.example: A major-general took command of the division.
items.exampleCN: 一位少将接管了这个师。

items.structure: major + domo (from Latin major domus 'chief of the household')
items.meaning: the chief servant managing a large household
items.meaningCN: 大管家；总管（原义“家宅之首”）
items.example: The majordomo greeted the guests at the door.
items.exampleCN: 大管家在门口迎接客人。

items.meaning: greater
items.example: The comparative is the direct source of major.
items.exampleCN: 这个比较级是 major 的直接来源。

items.meaning: great, large
items.example: The positive degree stands behind magnify and magnitude.
items.exampleCN: 这个原级支撑 magnify 与 magnitude。

items.meaning: greater (combining form)
items.example: The stem appears in major, majority and majesty.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干见于 major、majority 与 majesty。

items.meaning: quality or state
items.example: It forms majority, the greater part.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 majority，即较大部分。

items.meaning: a person of great wealth or power
items.example: A shipping magnate funded the library.
items.exampleCN: 一位航运巨头资助了这座图书馆。

latinEntries.meaning: to make something appear or become greater
latinEntries.meaningCN: 放大；夸大（使变大）

latinEntries.meaning: greatness of size, importance, or brightness
latinEntries.meaningCN: 巨大；重要性；星等（大小或程度的量）

latinEntries.meaning: a person with control, skill, or authority
latinEntries.meaningCN: 主人；大师；硕士（原指“更甚者、首领”）

latinEntries.meaning: royal dignity; grandeur
latinEntries.meaningCN: 威严；陛下（王室尊称，原义“伟大”）

definition_zh: （用手）熟练操作；摆弄；操控（他人）；篡改（数据）；操纵（市场、局势）
definition_en: to handle or control something skillfully with the hands or instruments, or to influence people, information, or markets in a controlled and often hidden way
core_image: 指腹捏住一团黏土，表面不动声色，形状却被一点点改成自己想要的样子
scene: 诊室里，医生让病人放松手腕。He used his thumb along the joint space to manipulate the small displaced joint and push it back into place.
sceneCN: 这里 manipulate 是「医疗手法复位」（第 3 个义项：用手法调整骨骼、关节）；句意：他用拇指沿骨缝把错位的小关节推回原位。图中可辨识物件：诊床、病人的手腕、医生的拇指、关节模型。

pos.zh: 熟练操作；摆弄；操控；篡改；操纵

collocations.zh: 把某人摆布得去做某事

derivatives.zh: 操作；操控；篡改；手法治疗
操纵他人的；控制的；手法操作的

senses.title: Skilled handling: shape something with the hands
senses.titleCN: 巧手处理：用手把材料做成形
senses.definition: to handle, move, or shape something skillfully with the hands
senses.definitionCN: 用手熟练地拿捏、移动或塑造某物
senses.example: The sculptor manipulated the wet clay into a narrow face.
senses.exampleCN: 雕塑家把湿黏土捏成一张瘦长的脸。
senses.why: Manipulate was back-formed from manipulation in 1827 and first meant 'to handle skillfully by hand'. The Latin source manipulus is literally 'a handful', so the hand is not a metaphor here but the original instrument.
senses.whyCN: manipulate 于 1827 年由 manipulation 逆构而来，最初意为“用手熟练处理”。拉丁语来源 manipulus 字面就是“一把”，所以这里的“手”不是比喻，而是最初的工具。

senses.title: Operate a tool or control with practiced skill
senses.titleCN: 熟练操作工具或控制装置
senses.definition: to operate a device, machine, or set of controls with learned skill
senses.definitionCN: 以习得的技巧操作装置、机器或一组控制件
senses.example: Only two technicians can manipulate the robotic arm safely.
senses.exampleCN: 只有两名技术员能安全地操作这条机械臂。
senses.why: Once the hand works through a tool, the skill moves from fingers to procedure. The object is no longer clay but a lever, a switch or a joystick, and manipulation becomes trained operation.
senses.whyCN: 当手通过工具工作时，技巧就从指尖转移到程序上。被处理的不再是黏土，而是操纵杆、开关或摇杆，manipulation 于是变成受过训练的操作。

senses.title: Medical handling: put a joint or bone back
senses.titleCN: 医疗手法：把关节或骨头归位
senses.definition: to adjust or reduce a joint, bone, or tissue by hand as a treatment
senses.definitionCN: 以手调整或复位关节、骨骼、组织，作为治疗手段
senses.example: The doctor manipulated the dislocated finger back into place.
senses.exampleCN: 医生把脱位的手指手法复位。
senses.why: Here the hand applies controlled force inside the body rather than on an object. The sense stays neutral and technical: manipulation in medicine is a procedure, not a trick.
senses.whyCN: 这里手在身体内部施加受控的力量，而不是作用在物体上。这个义项保持中性、技术化：医学里的 manipulation 是一项操作，而不是花招。

senses.title: Influence a person behind the surface
senses.titleCN: 在表面之下影响一个人
senses.definition: to influence a person's feelings or decisions in a hidden, indirect, often selfish way
senses.definitionCN: 以隐蔽、间接、常为私利的方式影响他人的情感或决定
senses.example: He manipulated his colleagues into supporting a plan they did not understand.
senses.exampleCN: 他摆布同事们去支持一个他们并不理解的计划。
senses.why: The sense 'to manage by mental influence, especially for one's own purposes' is recorded by 1864, after an 1828 extension to 'handling persons'. The hand now moves feelings instead of clay, and the hidden grip is what makes the word negative.
senses.whyCN: “以心理影响加以摆布，尤指为私利”的义项记录于 1864 年，此前 1828 年已从物件扩展到“摆布人”。此时手移动的是情绪而非黏土，那只看不见的手正是这个词带贬义的原因。

senses.title: Falsify information: make the record say what you want
senses.titleCN: 篡改信息：让记录说出自己想要的话
senses.definition: to change data, accounts, images, or records dishonestly so that they mislead
senses.definitionCN: 不诚实地改动数据、账目、图像或记录，使其误导他人
senses.example: The company manipulated its sales figures before the audit.
senses.exampleCN: 公司在审计前篡改了销售数字。
senses.why: Numbers are soft material for a skilled hand. The financial sense appears by 1870, and it keeps the original structure: a handful is quietly reshaped until the total looks right.
senses.whyCN: 数字对熟练的手而言是柔软的材料。金融义在 1870 年出现，保留了最初的结构：悄悄把“一把”数字捏到总数看起来正确为止。

senses.title: Rig a market or an outcome
senses.titleCN: 操纵市场或结果
senses.definition: to control prices, competition, or a result artificially, usually for profit
senses.definitionCN: 人为控制价格、竞争或结果，通常为获利
senses.example: Regulators found that traders had manipulated the price of electricity.
senses.exampleCN: 监管机构认定交易员操纵了电价。
senses.why: A market is a system of many hands, and manipulation means one hand quietly sets the scale for everyone else. The word still describes control exercised from behind, not open bargaining.
senses.whyCN: 市场是许多只手组成的系统，manipulation 意味着一只手悄悄替所有人定下刻度。这个词描述的仍是从背后施加的控制，而不是公开的讨价还价。

senses.title: Control variables in an experiment or system
senses.titleCN: 控制实验或系统中的变量
senses.definition: in science and computing, to change or control variables, parameters, or data structures deliberately
senses.definitionCN: 在科学与计算中，有意识地改变或控制变量、参数或数据结构
senses.example: The model lets researchers manipulate one variable while holding the rest fixed.
senses.exampleCN: 这个模型让研究者固定其余变量、只操纵一个变量。
senses.why: This is manipulation without deception: the hand is visible and the purpose is stated. The technical sense shows that the word's negativity comes from intent and concealment, not from control itself.
senses.whyCN: 这是没有欺骗的 manipulation：手是看得见的，目的也说明白。这个技术义说明，这个词的贬义来自意图与隐瞒，而不是来自“控制”本身。

senses.title: Usage boundary: neutral skill vs hidden control
senses.titleCN: 用法边界：中性技巧与暗中控制
senses.definition: manipulate can be neutral when the object is a material, tool, joint, or variable, but is pejorative when the object is a person, information, or a market; it is stronger and more secretive than handle or manage
senses.definitionCN: 当对象是材料、工具、关节或变量时可为中性；当对象是人、信息或市场时带贬义；它比 handle 或 manage 更强，也更强调暗中进行
senses.example: A surgeon manipulates tissue; a demagogue manipulates fear. The verb is the same, the ethics are not.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生 manipulate 组织；煽动者 manipulate 恐惧。动词相同，伦理不同。
senses.why: English kept one verb for both because the physical gesture is identical: a hand takes hold and directs. The usage note is the boundary: neutral when the object cannot consent, pejorative when it can.
senses.whyCN: 英语让同一个动词覆盖两者，因为手上的动作完全相同：一只手抓住并引导。用法要点就是那条边界：对象无法同意时是中性的，对象能同意时就是贬义的。

intro.en: Manipulate is a back-formation from manipulation, a word first used for handling ore. Its Latin core is manipulus 'a handful', from manus 'hand'. The second part of manipulus is often linked to 'fill', but that link is not certain.
intro.cn: manipulate 是由 manipulation 逆构而来的词，后者最初用于处理矿石。其拉丁核心是 manipulus“一把”，来自 manus“手”。manipulus 的第二部分常被联系到“填满”，但这一联系并不确定。

items.en: Manipulation is recorded by 1730 as a method of digging or handling ore, from French manipulation. The earliest English use is technical, not psychological.
items.cn: manipulation 于 1730 年记录为一种挖掘、处理矿石的方法，来自法语 manipulation。最早的英语用法是技术性的，而非心理层面的。

items.en: From Latin manipulus 'handful, sheaf, bundle', also a pharmacists' measure. The first element is manus 'hand'; the second is often connected with plere 'to fill', but the etymology of that second element is source uncertain.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 manipulus“一把、一束、一捆”，也是药剂师的量名。第一成分是 manus“手”；第二成分常与 plere“填满”联系，但该第二成分的词源来源不确定。

items.en: manus is traced to PIE *man- (2) 'hand'. This reconstruction is generally accepted. Because the second element of manipulus is uncertain, no full PIE shape should be asserted for the whole word.
items.cn: manus 被追溯到原始印欧语 *man-（第二支）“手”，这一重构属于一般认为。由于 manipulus 的第二成分不确定，不应为整词断言完整的原始印欧语形式。

items.en: Manipulate is recorded as a back-formation meaning 'to handle skillfully by hand'. The verb was cut from the noun, so the noun is older than the verb.
items.cn: manipulate 作为逆构词记录于 1827 年，意为“用手熟练处理”。动词是从名词上“切”下来的，因此名词比动词更早。

items.en: The sense extends to 'handling or managing persons' by 1828, to mental influence for one's own purposes by 1864, and to financial manipulation by 1870.
items.cn: 词义于 1828 年扩展到“摆布、管理人”，1864 年扩展到“为私利施加心理影响”，1870 年扩展到金融上的操纵。

items.en: Modern English uses one verb for the sculptor, the surgeon, the scientist, the fraudster and the demagogue. The neutral and the pejorative readings are separated by the object and by whether the control is admitted.
items.cn: 现代英语用同一个动词覆盖雕塑家、外科医生、科学家、造假者与煽动者。中性义与贬义由对象决定，也由这种控制是否被承认决定。

note.en: The first group shares the manus 'hand' family or the manip- shape. The second group separates physical handling, technical operation, neutral control and dishonest rigging.
note.cn: 第一组共享 manus“手”词族或 manip- 词形。第二组区分实体拿捏、技术操作、中性控制与不诚实的操纵。

entries.definition: the noun from manipulate: skilled handling, medical adjustment, or hidden control. It is older than the verb.
entries.definitionCN: manipulate 的名词：熟练操作、医疗手法或暗中操控。它比动词更早出现。

entries.definition: using hidden influence to control people. It almost always carries disapproval, unlike the neutral verb.
entries.definitionCN: 用隐蔽影响控制他人的。它几乎总带贬义，而动词本身可以是中性的。

entries.definition: care for the hands and nails. It joins manus 'hand' with cura 'care', a different second element from manipulus.
entries.definitionCN: 手部与指甲护理。它由 manus“手”+ cura“照料”构成，第二成分与 manipulus 不同。

entries.definition: to hold, move, or deal with something with the hands. It is neutral and lacks the hidden-control sense.
entries.definitionCN: 用手拿、移动或处理某物。它中性，没有“暗中控制”的含义。

entries.definition: to run a machine or system. It covers the technical sense of manipulate but says nothing about skill or secrecy.
entries.definitionCN: 操作机器或系统。它覆盖 manipulate 的技术义，但不含技巧高低或秘密性的意味。

entries.definition: to direct or limit something. It is broader and more neutral than manipulate, which implies indirect or unfair direction.
entries.definitionCN: 指挥或限制某事物。它比 manipulate 更宽、更中性，后者隐含间接或不正当的引导。

entries.definition: to arrange a competition, price, or vote dishonestly. It is narrower and more openly criminal than manipulate.
entries.definitionCN: 不诚实地安排比赛、价格或投票。它比 manipulate 更窄，也更明确指向违法。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: manus 'hand' gives manual, manuscript, manufacture and manicure; manipulus 'a handful' gives manipulate and manipulation.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词与真实同族词：manus“手”给出 manual、manuscript、manufacture、manicure；manipulus“一把”给出 manipulate 与 manipulation。

normal.en: manipulus is 'a handful'. Manipulate began as the act of working a handful of material, and the hand stayed in the word.
normal.cn: manipulus 就是“一把”。manipulate 最初是处理“一把”材料的动作，那只手一直留在词里。

normal.en: The noun came first: manipulation (1730, ore handling), then the verb manipulate (1827). The verb was cut down from the noun.
normal.cn: 名词先出现：manipulation（1730，处理矿石），然后才是动词 manipulate（1827）。动词是从名词上截下来的。

normal.en: Medical manipulation is neutral: a hand puts a joint back. The same word turns negative only when the hand works on a mind or a record.
normal.cn: 医学上的 manipulation 是中性的：手把关节归位。只有当这只手作用于头脑或记录时，同一个词才转为贬义。

normal.en: Manipulate data and manipulate public opinion share one image: adjusting the material until the result looks natural.
normal.cn: manipulate data 与 manipulate public opinion 共享一个意象：把材料调到结果看起来自然为止。

normal.en: Manicure, manual and manuscript all contain manus 'hand': nail care, hand work, and a book small enough for one hand.
normal.cn: manicure、manual、manuscript 都含 manus“手”：指甲护理、手工操作，以及一只手就能拿的小书。

abstract.en: Picture a hand under a cloth moving pieces on a board. Everyone sees the board; no one sees the fingers. Manipulate is control whose source stays out of sight.
abstract.cn: 想象一块布下有一只手在挪动棋盘上的棋子。所有人都看见棋盘，没人看见手指。manipulate 就是来源始终藏在视线之外的控制。

abstract.en: The same grip works on clay, a lever, a joint, a number, a price or a feeling. The material changes; the quiet adjusting does not.
abstract.cn: 同一种捏握可以作用于黏土、操纵杆、关节、数字、价格或情绪。材料在变，那种无声的调整没有变。

abstract.en: When the object can say no, the hand becomes a moral problem; when it cannot, the hand is only skill. That line runs through every sense.
abstract.cn: 当对象能说“不”时，这只手就成了道德问题；当对象不能说“不”时，这只手只是技巧。这条线贯穿所有义项。

examples.en: The puppeteer manipulates the strings with two fingers.
examples.cn: 木偶师用两根手指操纵提线。

examples.en: The audit showed that several entries had been manipulated.
examples.cn: 审计显示有多笔账目被篡改过。

examples.en: Advertisers manipulate desire long before they mention the product.
examples.cn: 广告商在提到产品之前，早就在操控欲望了。

dict_mnemonic.text: “马尼扑雷特”——马尼一把扑住雷特的手腕，把他摆布得团团转 → manipulate 摆弄、操控

root: 由 manipulation 逆构；拉丁语 manipulus“一把、一束”来自 manus“手”，核心是“用手握住材料并加以摆弄、引导”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of manipulate, one hand at work: shaping clay, operating a control, setting a joint, steering a person, rewriting a record, rigging a market, holding a variable fixed, and the boundary where skill becomes manipulation.
sensesIntro.cn: manipulate 的八个义项都是同一只手在工作：捏黏土、扳操纵杆、复位关节、牵引他人、改写记录、操纵市场、固定变量，以及技巧变成“操控”的那条边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand takes hold of material and quietly directs its shape.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手握住材料，悄悄决定它的形状。

branches.en: MATERIAL AND TOOL: clay and controls are both held and moved by practiced fingers.
branches.cn: 材料与工具：黏土和操纵装置都是被熟练手指握住并移动的对象。

branches.en: BODY: the hand works inside the body, but as a neutral medical procedure.
branches.cn: 身体：手在身体内部工作，但作为中性的医疗程序。

branches.en: MIND: the grip moves to feelings and decisions, and concealment makes it negative.
branches.cn: 心智：捏握转向情感与决定，隐瞒使它变成贬义。

branches.en: RECORDS AND MARKETS: numbers and prices are soft material, reshaped until the result looks natural.
branches.cn: 记录与市场：数字和价格是柔软的材料，被捏到结果看起来自然为止。

branches.en: SYSTEMS AND BOUNDARY: a declared variable is neutral control, and the object decides whether the word is an accusation.
branches.cn: 系统与边界：公开说明的变量是中性的控制，而对象决定这个词是否是指控。

intro.en: Manipulate has no live English prefix. Its Latin core manipulus is frozen inside, and English adds only -ion, -ive, -or and -able to the finished verb.
intro.cn: manipulate 没有活的英语前缀。它的拉丁核心 manipulus 凝固在词内，英语只在成品动词后加 -ion、-ive、-or、-able。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on manus 'hand': manual and manuscript work by hand, manufacture is made by hand, and manicure cares for the hand. Manipulus adds the 'handful' measure.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族建立在 manus“手”上：manual 与 manuscript 与手有关，manufacture 是“手做”，manicure 是照料手。manipulus 再加上“一把”这个量。

items.structure: Latin manipulus (handful) + -ation (noun of action); the verb is a back-formation
items.meaning: the act of handling skillfully, adjusting by hand, or controlling dishonestly
items.meaningCN: 操作；手法调整；操控（-ion 构成行为名词）
items.example: Careful manipulation of the evidence was later exposed.
items.exampleCN: 对证据的精心篡改后来被揭露了。

items.meaning: tending to control people indirectly and unfairly
items.meaningCN: 善于操控他人的；工于心计的（-ive 表示倾向）
items.example: His manipulative emails made the team distrust him.
items.exampleCN: 他那些操控性的邮件让团队不再信任他。

items.meaning: a person who controls others, or a device for handling objects
items.meaningCN: 操纵者；操作器；机械手（-or 表示做该动作的人或装置）
items.example: The remote manipulator picks up samples in the glove box.
items.exampleCN: 遥控机械手在手套箱里取样。

items.meaning: able to be handled or controlled
items.meaningCN: 可操作的；可被操控的（-able 表示“能够被……”）
items.example: In this model every parameter is manipulable.
items.exampleCN: 在这个模型里，每个参数都可以被操纵。

items.meaning: hand
items.example: The hand is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: “手”是整个词族的基础。

items.meaning: a handful; a bundle
items.example: The noun gave the verb its image of handling.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词给动词“握持”的意象。

items.meaning: to make, to act
items.example: It forms the verb from the noun of handling.
items.exampleCN: 它由“握持”名词构成动词。

items.meaning: an act or its result
items.example: It forms manipulation, the act of handling.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 manipulation，即操控行为。

items.meaning: a handful; a small detachment of soldiers
items.meaningCN: 一小队士兵；（祭司佩戴的）饰带
items.example: The Roman maniple was a small tactical unit.
items.exampleCN: 罗马的 maniple 是一个小型战术单位。

latinEntries.meaning: done by hand; a handbook small enough to hold
latinEntries.meaningCN: 手工的；手册（原义“可一手拿的小书”）

latinEntries.meaning: a document written by hand rather than printed
latinEntries.meaningCN: 手稿；手写本（手写的文字）

latinEntries.meaning: to make goods, originally by hand
latinEntries.meaningCN: 制造（原义“用手做”）

latinEntries.meaning: care for the hands and nails
latinEntries.meaningCN: 手部护理；修指甲（照料手）

definition_zh: 手工的；手动的；体力的；手册；手动挡汽车；手键盘
definition_en: done or operated by the hands rather than by machine or automatically; as a noun, a book of instructions, a hand-played keyboard, or a car with a manual gearbox
core_image: 一只沾着机油的手掌托着一本薄册：既能亲手操作，也能一手拿起
scene: 修车铺里，技师翻开油污的手册。He opened the oily manual to page forty-two and tightened the bolts with a hand wrench, following the drawing exactly.
sceneCN: 这里 manual 是「手册」（第 4 个义项：一手可持的手册）；句意：他翻开油污的手册到第 42 页，照图示用手动扳手拧紧螺栓。图中可辨识物件：维修手册、扳手、发动机舱、螺栓。

pos.zh: 手工的；手动的；体力的
手册；说明书；手动挡；手键盘

derivatives.zh: 手语教学法；主张手工训练的教育观点
主张手工训练者；手语教学者
手册化的；按手册标准化操作的

senses.title: Done with the hands, not by machine
senses.titleCN: 用手完成，而非机器完成
senses.definition: done, made, or performed with the hands rather than by machine or tool
senses.definitionCN: 用手而不是机器或工具完成、制作或执行
senses.example: The wall was built by manual labour, stone by stone.
senses.exampleCN: 这堵墙是靠手工劳动一块石头一块石头砌成的。
senses.why: Latin manualis meant 'of or belonging to the hand', from manus 'hand'. The adjective's first job in English, around 1400, was to mark work done by hand, so the hand is the defining instrument.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 manualis 意为“属于手的”，来自 manus“手”。这个形容词约在 1400 年进入英语时的第一项任务，就是标记“用手完成的工作”，因此手是定义性的工具。

senses.title: Hand-operated: a control that bypasses the machine
senses.titleCN: 手动操作：绕开自动装置的控制
senses.definition: of a device or control, operated by physical hand movement rather than automatically
senses.definitionCN: 指装置或控制件靠手的实际动作操作，而不是自动运行
senses.example: If the sensor fails, use the manual override beside the door.
senses.exampleCN: 如果传感器失灵，就用门旁的手动超控装置。
senses.why: Here the contrast is not hand versus machine in general but hand versus automatic. A manual switch exists so that a person can take over from the system, which is why manual also means 'not automatic'.
senses.whyCN: 这里对比的不是泛泛的“手与机器”，而是“手动与自动”。手动开关的存在，就是为了让人能从系统手里接管，因此 manual 也引申为“非自动的”。

senses.title: Physical rather than mental work
senses.titleCN: 体力工作，而非脑力工作
senses.definition: of work or a worker, involving bodily effort rather than office or intellectual work
senses.definitionCN: 指工作或劳动者需要体力，而不是办公室或脑力工作
senses.example: The factory replaced most manual jobs with automated lines.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂用自动化生产线取代了大多数体力岗位。
senses.why: The hand is the body's most obvious working part, so manual work became a social category opposed to head work. The word now describes a class of employment, not just a method.
senses.whyCN: 手是身体最明显的工作部位，因此 manual work 成了与“脑力工作”相对的社会类别。这个词现在描述的是一类就业，而不只是一种方法。

senses.title: The handbook you hold in one hand
senses.titleCN: 一手可持的手册
senses.definition: a book giving instructions, rules, or reference information for a device, course, or job
senses.definitionCN: 为装置、课程或工作提供说明、规则或参考信息的书
senses.example: Read the manual before you change the filter.
senses.exampleCN: 换滤芯之前先读说明书。
senses.why: The noun is recorded in the early 15c. for a small service book, and by the 1530s for any concise handbook. The etymological picture is a small book that can be carried or used in one hand — the same hand returns.
senses.whyCN: 名词义在 15 世纪早期记录为小型的礼仪书，16 世纪 30 年代起指任何简明手册。词源画面是一本可以随身携带、或一手使用的小书——同一只手又回来了。

senses.title: A car you shift yourself
senses.titleCN: 自己换挡的车
senses.definition: in informal use, a car with a manual gearbox, as opposed to an automatic
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指带手动变速器的汽车，与自动挡相对
senses.example: I learned to drive on a manual and still prefer one.
senses.exampleCN: 我是开手动挡学会开车的，现在仍然更喜欢手动挡。
senses.why: The adjective manual transmission is shortened to the noun 'a manual'. The hand is now on the gear lever, so the word names the car by the kind of control it demands.
senses.whyCN: 形容词短语 manual transmission 被缩略成名词 a manual。此时手放在换挡杆上，于是这个词用“它要求哪种控制方式”来给车命名。

senses.title: The keyboard played by hand
senses.titleCN: 用手演奏的键盘
senses.definition: one of the hand-played keyboards of an organ, as opposed to the pedal keyboard
senses.definitionCN: 管风琴上用手演奏的键盘之一，与脚踏键盘相对
senses.example: The organist moves between the swell manual and the great manual.
senses.exampleCN: 管风琴手在强弱手键盘与主手键盘之间切换。
senses.why: In organ music, manuals are the rows played by hand and the pedals are played by foot. The adjective becomes a noun because the hand is what distinguishes this keyboard from the other.
senses.whyCN: 在管风琴音乐中，manual 是用手弹的键盘排，pedal 是用脚踩的。形容词转为名词，因为“用手”正是这组键盘区别于另一组的地方。

senses.title: The prescribed drill: manual exercise
senses.titleCN: 规定的操练：军事手册操典
senses.definition: in military history, the prescribed routine for handling a rifle or weapon, known as manual exercise
senses.definitionCN: 军事史上规定的步枪或武器操作程序，称为 manual exercise
senses.example: Recruits spent a week learning the manual exercise.
senses.exampleCN: 新兵花了一周学习武器操作操典。
senses.why: Manual exercise is recorded in 1760 as 'the art of handling the rifle and other arms with precision and according to the prescribed method'. Here manual means a fixed sequence performed by hand, not a book.
senses.whyCN: manual exercise 记录于 1760 年，意为“按既定方法精确操作步枪及其他武器的技艺”。这里的 manual 指的是一套用手完成的固定程序，而不是一本书。

senses.title: Usage boundary: manual, hand-made, menial
senses.titleCN: 用法边界：manual、hand-made、menial
senses.definition: manual describes hand operation or a handbook; it does not automatically mean unskilled or low-status, and manual is not a synonym of menial
senses.definitionCN: manual 描述用手操作或手册；它不自动表示“无需技能”或“地位低”，也不是 menial 的同义词
senses.example: Manual work can be highly skilled: a watchmaker's hands are manual and expert.
senses.exampleCN: 体力/手工工作也可以高度专业化：制表师的手既是 manual 的，也是专业的。
senses.why: Manual names the instrument (the hand), while menial names the status (low, servile). A manual job may be skilled, and a menial job may involve little handwork at all. The boundary keeps the word technical rather than social.
senses.whyCN: manual 命名的是工具（手），menial 命名的是地位（低微、仆役性）。manual 的工作可能很专业，menial 的工作可能根本不需要多少手工。这条边界让这个词保持技术性，而不是社会评判。

intro.en: Manual is the Latin adjective for 'of the hand'. English first used it for hand-made work, then for hand-operated controls, and turned it into a noun for a small book that fits in one hand — the same hand at both ends.
intro.cn: manual 是拉丁语中表示“属于手的”形容词。英语先用它表示手工完成的工作，再表示手动控制，随后转为名词，指一本能拿在一只手里的小书——两端都是同一只手。

items.en: First recorded as an adjective meaning 'of or pertaining to the hand; done, made, or used by hand', from Latin manualis.
items.cn: 约 1400 年首次记录为形容词，意为“属于手的；用手完成、制作或使用的”，来自拉丁语 manualis。

items.en: Latin manualis 'of or belonging to the hand; that can be thrown by hand', from manus 'hand, strength, power over; armed force; handwriting'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 manualis“属于手的；可以用手投掷的”，来自 manus“手、力量、支配权、武装力量、笔迹”。

items.en: manus is traced to PIE *man- (2) 'hand', the root also listed for manual, manage and manipulate. The reconstruction is generally accepted.
items.cn: manus 被追溯到原始印欧语 *man-（第二支）“手”，也是 manual、manage、manipulate 所列的词根。该重构属于一般认为。

items.en: The noun appears meaning 'small service book used by a priest', from Old French manuel 'handbook' and Late Latin manuale 'case or cover of a book, handbook'.
items.cn: 名词义出现，指“神父使用的小型礼仪书”，来自古法语 manuel“手册”与晚期拉丁语 manuale“书套或书封、手册”。

items.en: The meaning 'a concise handbook of any sort' is recorded from the 1530s. Manual exercise, the prescribed handling of a rifle, appears in 1760.
items.cn: “任何类型的简明手册”义记录于 16 世纪 30 年代。manual exercise（规定的步枪操作）出现于 1760 年。

items.en: Modern English uses manual for hand operation, physical work, a handbook, a manual gearbox and an organ keyboard. The common thread is the hand, not a single object.
items.cn: 现代英语用 manual 表示手动操作、体力工作、手册、手动挡和管风琴手键盘。共同线索是“手”，而不是某一个固定物件。

note.en: The first group shares manus 'hand' or the manual shape. The second group separates the book sense from the hand-operated sense, which English keeps inside one word.
note.cn: 第一组共享 manus“手”或 manual 的词形。第二组把“书”的义项与“用手操作”的义项分开，而英语把它们放在同一个词里。

entries.definition: a metal ring for the wrist; to chain someone. It comes from Latin manicula, a diminutive of manus 'hand'.
entries.definitionCN: 手铐；给某人上镣铐。它来自拉丁语 manicula，是 manus“手”的指小形式。

entries.definition: a text written by hand rather than printed. It joins manus 'hand' with scriptum 'written'.
entries.definitionCN: 手写而非印刷的文本。它由 manus“手”+ scriptum“写”构成。

entries.definition: by hand, by means of the hand. It is the adverb from manual, recorded in the late 15c.
entries.definitionCN: 用手地；靠手完成地。它是 manual 的副词，记录于 15 世纪晚期。

entries.definition: a concise reference book. It is the closest synonym of manual in the book sense, and itself translates Latin manualis.
entries.definitionCN: 简明参考书。它是 manual 在“书”这一义项上最接近的同义词，本身正是对拉丁语 manualis 的翻译。

entries.definition: a book or person that shows the way. It is broader than manual: a guide may describe a city, while a manual explains how to operate something.
entries.definitionCN: 指路的书或人。它比 manual 更宽：guide 可以介绍一座城市，而 manual 说明如何操作某物。

entries.definition: worked by hand rather than automatically. It overlaps manual in the device sense but cannot mean a handbook.
entries.definitionCN: 用手而非自动操作的。它在装置义上与 manual 重叠，但不能表示手册。

entries.definition: relating to the body rather than the mind. Manual work is always physical, but physical work need not use the hands.
entries.definitionCN: 与身体而非心智有关。manual 工作一定是体力/身体的，但体力工作不一定用手。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: manus 'hand' is the whole story, and it also appears in manuscript, manufacture, manicure, manacle and manage.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词与真实同族词：manus“手”就是全部故事，它也出现在 manuscript、manufacture、manicure、manacle、manage 里。

normal.en: manualis is 'of the hand'. Manual labour is work of the hand; a manual is a book small enough for the hand; a manual gearbox is shifted by hand.
normal.cn: manualis 就是“属于手的”。manual labour 是手的劳动；manual 是一本一手可拿的书；manual gearbox 是用手换挡的变速箱。

normal.en: Hand and book meet in the noun: the etymological sense of manual is 'a small book such as may be carried in the hand'.
normal.cn: 手与书在名词义里相遇：manual 的词源义就是“一本可以拿在手里携带的小书”。

normal.en: Manual exercise (1760) is a fixed sequence of hand movements with a rifle, so manual can name a drill as well as a book.
normal.cn: manual exercise（1760）是一套用步枪完成的固定手部动作，所以 manual 也能指操典，而不只是书。

normal.en: Manual override exists so a person can take control back from an automatic system: manual means 'the human hand is still allowed in'.
normal.cn: manual override 的存在，是为了让人能从自动系统手里夺回控制权：manual 意味着“人的手仍然被允许介入”。

normal.en: Manuscript, manufacture and manicure all use manus: writing by hand, making by hand, caring for the hand.
normal.cn: manuscript、manufacture、manicure 都用 manus：手写、手做、照料手。

abstract.en: Picture a hand and a thin book: the hand can work without the book, and the book can be held by the hand. Manual lives where the two meet.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手和一本薄书：手可以不用书就工作，书可以被手拿着。manual 就活在这两者相遇的地方。

abstract.en: The same word covers the tool (hand), the mode (manual operation), the guide (handbook) and the object (a manual car). The hand is the hinge.
abstract.cn: 同一个词覆盖工具（手）、方式（手动操作）、指南（手册）和物件（手动挡车）。手就是那个铰链。

abstract.en: When a machine automates the hand, manual becomes the exception that lets the hand return — a switch, a lever, an override.
abstract.cn: 当机器替代了手，manual 就成了让手回来的例外——一个开关、一根拉杆、一次超控。

examples.en: The manual explains how to reset the device in four steps.
examples.cn: 这本手册用四个步骤说明如何重置设备。

examples.en: Manual work is cheaper here, but slower than the new machine.
examples.cn: 这里的手工劳动更便宜，但比新机器慢。

examples.en: He prefers a manual because he likes choosing the gear.
examples.cn: 他更喜欢手动挡，因为他喜欢自己选挡位。

dict_mnemonic.text: “曼牛”——慢悠悠的牛拉着手工犁，旁边放着一本操作手册 → manual 手工的、手册

root: 拉丁语 manualis“属于手的”，来自 manus“手”，核心是“用手完成、用手操作”，并引申为“一手可持的小书”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of manual, all centred on the hand: work done by hand, a hand control, physical labour, a handbook held in one hand, a manual car, an organ keyboard, a rifle drill, and the boundary against menial.
sensesIntro.cn: manual 的八个义项都围绕手：用手完成的工作、手动控制、体力劳动、一手可持的手册、手动挡汽车、管风琴手键盘、步枪操典，以及它与 menial 的边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand does the work, and a thin book fits into that same hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：手完成工作，而一本薄书正好放进同一只手里。

branches.en: METHOD: work is done by hand rather than by machine.
branches.cn: 方式：工作靠手完成，而不是靠机器。

branches.en: CONTROL: a switch, a gear lever, an organ keyboard and a rifle drill all place the hand on a control.
branches.cn: 控制：开关、换挡杆、管风琴键盘与步枪操典，都把放在控制件上的手作为核心。

branches.en: LABOUR: handwork becomes a social category opposed to mental or office work.
branches.cn: 劳动：手工成为与脑力或办公室工作相对的社会类别。

branches.en: BOOK: a handbook is defined by being small enough to hold and use in one hand.
branches.cn: 书：手册之所以是手册，在于它小到可以一手拿着使用。

branches.en: BOUNDARY: manual names the instrument, not the status, so it never becomes menial by itself.
branches.cn: 边界：manual 命名工具，不命名地位，因此它本身从不等于 menial。

intro.en: Manual has no live English prefix. Its Latin stem manualis is frozen inside; English adds -ly, -ism and -ist, and forms compounds such as manual transmission and manual override.
intro.cn: manual 没有活的英语前缀。它的拉丁词干 manualis 凝固在词内；英语加 -ly、-ism、-ist，并构成 manual transmission、manual override 这类复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on manus 'hand': manuscript is hand-written, manufacture is hand-made, manicure is hand-care, and manacle is a hand-ring.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族建立在 manus“手”上：manuscript 是手写，manufacture 是手做，manicure 是照料手，manacle 是套手的环。

items.meaning: by hand, by means of the hand
items.meaningCN: 用手地；手动地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The valve must be closed manually.
items.exampleCN: 这个阀门必须手动关闭。

items.meaning: the practice or doctrine of teaching deaf people by hand signs, or of emphasizing manual training
items.meaningCN: 手语教学法；强调手工训练的主张（-ism 构成做法或主义）
items.example: Manualism competed with oralism in deaf education.
items.exampleCN: 在聋人教育中，手语教学法曾与口语教学法竞争。

items.meaning: a supporter of manual training or of hand-sign teaching
items.meaningCN: 主张手工训练者；手语教学者（-ist 表示实践者或支持者）
items.example: The manualists argued for keeping sign language in class.
items.exampleCN: 手语教学派主张在课堂上保留手语。

items.meaning: standardized according to a written manual, especially in therapy or research
items.meaningCN: 按书面手册标准化的（-ize 表示“使……化”，-ed 构成形容词）
items.example: The treatment was manualized so that every clinic followed the same steps.
items.exampleCN: 这种治疗被手册化了，好让每家诊所都按同样步骤执行。

items.meaning: hand
items.example: The hand is the base of manual and manuscript.
items.exampleCN: “手”是 manual 与 manuscript 的基础。

items.meaning: by hand (combining form)
items.example: The form appears in manumit and manufacture.
items.exampleCN: 这个形式见于 manumit 与 manufacture。

items.meaning: relating to
items.example: It makes the adjective manual from the hand noun.
items.exampleCN: 它由“手”构成形容词 manual。

items.meaning: to handle skillfully; to control
items.example: The same hand root built manipulate.
items.exampleCN: 同一个“手”词根也构成了 manipulate。

latinEntries.meaning: a text written by hand
latinEntries.meaningCN: 手稿；手写本

latinEntries.meaning: to make goods, originally by hand
latinEntries.meaningCN: 制造（原义“用手做”）

latinEntries.meaning: care for the hands and nails
latinEntries.meaningCN: 手部护理；修指甲

latinEntries.meaning: a ring for the hand; a handcuff
latinEntries.meaningCN: 手铐（套在手的小环）

definition_zh: 边缘；页边空白；差额；余地；利润空间；保证金
definition_en: the edge of an area, the blank space around printed text, the amount by which one thing differs from another, or the spare room kept for safety or profit
core_image: 纸页四周留出的白边：文字被围在中央，四周空着，可以写批注，也可以留作退路
scene: 编辑把校样摊在桌上。She wrote a note in red in the right margin, asking the author to delete a repeated sentence.
sceneCN: 这里 margin 是「页边空白」（第 2 个义项：书页文字四周的空白）；句意：她在右侧页边空白处用红笔写下一行批注，请作者删去重复的句子。图中可辨识物件：校样纸、红色批注、页边白区、钢笔。

pos.zh: 边缘；页边空白；差额；余地；利润；保证金
在页边加批注；给……留边

collocations.zh: 以保证金买进（融资买入）

forms.label: 三单（动词，与名词复数同形）

derivatives.zh: 页边的；边缘的；微小的；边际的
使边缘化；排挤到次要位置

senses.title: The edge of a physical area
senses.titleCN: 实体区域的边缘
senses.definition: the outer edge or border of a sea, lake, forest, field, or other area
senses.definitionCN: 海、湖、森林、田野或其他区域的外缘或边界
senses.example: Tall reeds grow along the margin of the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 高高的芦苇长在湖的边缘。
senses.why: Margin is first recorded in the mid-14c. as 'edge of a sea or lake'. Latin margo meant 'edge, brink, border', so the word starts at the outermost line where one area stops and another begins.
senses.whyCN: margin 最早记录于 14 世纪中期，意为“海或湖的边缘”。拉丁语 margo 意为“边缘、崖边、边界”，因此这个词的起点是一个区域终止、另一个区域开始的那条最外线。

senses.title: The blank space around a page of text
senses.titleCN: 书页文字四周的空白
senses.definition: the blank space between a block of text and the edge of a page
senses.definitionCN: 一块文字与纸张边缘之间的空白区域
senses.example: She wrote questions in the margin beside each paragraph.
senses.exampleCN: 她在每段旁边的页边空白处写下问题。
senses.why: By the late 14c. the word was used for the space between text and the edge of a leaf or sheet. The margin is not where writing ends but the reserved emptiness around it, which is why notes can later be added there.
senses.whyCN: 到 14 世纪晚期，这个词已用于指文字与纸页边缘之间的空间。页边不是文字结束的地方，而是文字周围被预留的空白，因此后来可以在那里加批注。

senses.title: The gap that decides a contest
senses.titleCN: 决定胜负的差距
senses.definition: the amount by which one competitor, result, or number is greater or smaller than another
senses.definitionCN: 一个竞争者、结果或数字比另一个大或小的量
senses.example: The bill passed by a margin of three votes.
senses.exampleCN: 这项法案以三票的差距通过。
senses.why: Two results sit side by side, and the margin is the strip of space between them. A narrow margin means the strip is thin, so the outcome could easily have gone the other way.
senses.whyCN: 两个结果并排放着，margin 就是两者之间那条空隙。narrow margin 意味着这条缝隙很窄，所以结果很容易倒向另一边。

senses.title: Spare room kept for safety
senses.titleCN: 为安全预留的余地
senses.definition: an amount of time, money, or tolerance kept free so that unexpected problems can be absorbed
senses.definitionCN: 预留出的时间、金钱或容差，用来吸收意外问题
senses.example: Leave a margin of ten minutes before the connecting train.
senses.exampleCN: 给换乘列车留出十分钟的余量。
senses.why: The sense 'comfort allowance, cushion, scope, provision for extended action' is recorded by 1851, and margin of error by 1889. A page margin protects the text; a safety margin protects the plan.
senses.whyCN: “舒适的余量、缓冲、活动空间、为扩大行动所作的预留”这一义项记录于 1851 年，margin of error 记录于 1889 年。页边保护文字，安全余量保护计划。

senses.title: The strip between cost and price
senses.titleCN: 成本与售价之间的那一条
senses.definition: the difference between the cost of producing or buying something and the price at which it is sold
senses.definitionCN: 生产或购买某物的成本与售价之间的差额
senses.example: The bakery survives on a thin profit margin.
senses.exampleCN: 这家面包店靠很薄的利润空间维持。
senses.why: In business the two sides of the page become cost and price, and the margin is the space between them. A thin margin leaves little room for error, which connects the financial sense back to the safety sense.
senses.whyCN: 在商业里，纸页的两边变成成本与售价，margin 就是两者之间的空间。薄利意味着几乎没有犯错的余地，这把金融义重新连回“安全余量”义。

senses.title: Collateral deposited with a broker
senses.titleCN: 交给经纪人的保证金
senses.definition: money deposited with a broker to cover the risk of loss when buying securities or goods on credit
senses.definitionCN: 以保证金方式买证券或货物时，交给经纪人以覆盖亏损风险的钱
senses.example: He bought the shares on margin and had to add cash after the drop.
senses.exampleCN: 他以保证金买进股票，股价下跌后不得不追加现金。
senses.why: The stock-market sense is recorded from 1848. The deposit is a buffer placed between the trader and a possible loss, exactly like the blank space that keeps the text from the edge.
senses.whyCN: 股市义记录于 1848 年。这笔押金是放在交易者与可能亏损之间的缓冲，和把文字与纸边隔开的空白完全同构。

senses.title: The edge of society: unimportant position
senses.titleCN: 社会的边缘：不重要的位置
senses.definition: a position at the edge of a group or society, with little influence or recognition
senses.definitionCN: 处于群体或社会边缘的位置，影响力或受认可度很低
senses.example: The report focuses on families living on the margins of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告关注生活在城市边缘的家庭。
senses.why: A page has a centre and a margin, and a society can be imagined the same way. The adjective marginal, 'of little effect or importance', is recorded from 1887, so the spatial word becomes a social judgement.
senses.whyCN: 一页纸有中心也有页边，一个社会也可以被这样想象。形容词 marginal“影响很小、不重要”记录于 1887 年，于是空间词变成了社会判断。

senses.title: To write in the margin
senses.titleCN: 在页边写字
senses.definition: to add notes in the margin of a page, or to provide something with a margin
senses.definitionCN: 在书页边缘添加批注，或给某物留出边
senses.example: The student margined every chapter with questions.
senses.exampleCN: 这个学生在每一章的页边都写满了问题。
senses.why: The verb appears c. 1600 as 'to furnish with marginal notes', and from 1715 as 'to furnish with a margin'. The place becomes an action: the blank strip is put to use.
senses.whyCN: 动词义约在 1600 年出现，意为“加页边注”，1715 年起又表示“给……留边”。地点变成了动作：那条空白被用起来了。

senses.title: Usage boundary: margin is not edge, profit, or leeway
senses.titleCN: 用法边界：margin 不等于 edge、profit 或 leeway
senses.definition: margin usually implies reserved or measured space, not a hard boundary; profit margin is a ratio, not the profit itself; margins in finance are collateral, not earnings
senses.definitionCN: margin 通常暗示被预留或被量出的空间，而不是硬边界；profit margin 是比率，不是利润本身；金融里的 margins 是保证金，不是收益
senses.example: The company's margin is thin, but its total profit is still large.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司的利润率很薄，但利润总额仍然很大。
senses.why: Edge is simply where something stops; margin is the strip left around it. Profit is the money kept; a profit margin is the proportion that money represents. Keeping these apart prevents 'a large margin' from being read as 'a large profit'.
senses.whyCN: edge 只是某物终止的地方；margin 是围绕它留下的那一条。profit 是留下的钱；profit margin 是这笔钱所占的比例。分清这些，才不会把“a large margin”误读成“a large profit”。

intro.en: Margin began as the physical edge of water or land, then became the blank strip around printed text. From that strip came the ideas of a gap between results, spare room for safety, and the difference between cost and price.
intro.cn: margin 最初指水域或陆地的实体边缘，随后变成印刷文字四周的空白条。从这条空白又衍生出结果之间的差距、为安全预留的余量，以及成本与售价之间的差额。

items.en: First recorded as 'edge of a sea or lake', from Old French margin and directly from Latin marginem (nominative margo) 'edge, brink, border, margin'.
items.cn: 最早记录为“海或湖的边缘”，来自古法语 margin，并直接来自拉丁语 marginem（主格 margo）“边缘、崖边、边界、页边”。

items.en: The sense 'space between a block of text and the edge of a leaf or sheet' appears. The general sense 'bordering space, boundary space, rim or edge' follows in the same period.
items.cn: “文字块与纸页边缘之间的空间”义出现。“边界空间、边缘、外缘”的一般义也在同一时期出现。

items.en: margo is traced to PIE *merg- 'boundary, border'. The reconstruction is generally accepted; the root is also associated with mark and march, though those reach English by other routes.
items.cn: margo 被追溯到原始印欧语 *merg-“边界、边缘”。这一重构属于一般认为；该词根也与 mark、march 有关，但后两者经其他路径进入英语。

items.en: The stock-market sense 'sum deposited with a broker to cover risk of loss' is recorded from 1848, the earliest of the modern figurative senses.
items.cn: 股市义“交给经纪人以覆盖亏损风险的押金”记录于 1848 年，是现代引申义中最早的一个。

items.en: The sense 'comfort allowance, cushion, scope, range' is recorded by 1851, and margin of error by 1889. Marginal, 'of little effect or importance', follows in 1887.
items.cn: “舒适余量、缓冲、活动空间、范围”义记录于 1851 年，margin of error 记录于 1889 年。marginal“影响很小、不重要”随后于 1887 年出现。

items.en: Modern English keeps the page sense, adds profit margin and social margins, and keeps the verb meaning 'to annotate'. The core idea is always reserved space between two things.
items.cn: 现代英语保留页边义，增加利润率与社会边缘义，并保留动词“加旁注”义。核心始终是两样东西之间被预留的空间。

note.en: The first group is built on margo or the margin shape. The second group separates the physical edge, the dividing line, the financial gain and the freedom to act.
note.cn: 第一组建立在 margo 或 margin 词形上。第二组区分实体边缘、分界线、财务收益与行动自由。

entries.definition: written in a margin, at the edge, or too small to matter. It is the adjective from margin, recorded from the 1570s.
entries.definitionCN: 写在页边的、位于边缘的，或小到不重要的。它是 margin 的形容词，记录于 16 世纪 70 年代。

entries.definition: notes written in the margins of a book. It is the plural of the Latin neuter marginalis.
entries.definitionCN: 写在书页边上的批注。它是拉丁语中性形式 marginalis 的复数。

entries.definition: a poetic or old-fashioned word for edge or margin. It is easily confused with margarine, which is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 诗歌或旧式用语中的“边缘”。它容易被误认成 margarine（人造黄油），后者与此无关。

entries.definition: the line where a surface ends. It is sharper and more literal than margin, which often implies a strip of reserved space.
entries.definitionCN: 一个表面终止的那条线。它比 margin 更锋利、更字面；margin 常暗示一条被预留的空间。

entries.definition: the line dividing two countries or regions. It is political or geographic, while margin is usually a space rather than a line.
entries.definitionCN: 分隔两国或两地区的界线。它是政治或地理的；margin 通常是空间，而不是一条线。

entries.definition: the money left after costs are paid. A profit margin is the ratio, not the sum, so the two are not interchangeable.
entries.definitionCN: 付完成本后剩下的钱。profit margin 是比率而不是金额，两者不能互换。

entries.definition: the freedom to act or to be late without punishment. Margin is the spare amount; leeway is the permission to use it.
entries.definitionCN: 行动的自由，或可迟到而不受罚的宽容度。margin 是预留的量；leeway 是使用这个量的许可。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: margo 'edge' gives margin and marginal; the blank strip on a page is the image behind every later financial and social sense.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词与真实同族词：margo“边缘”给出 margin 与 marginal；纸页上的空白条是后来所有金融义与社会义的底层意象。

normal.en: Look at a printed page: the text sits in the middle and a white strip runs around it. That strip is the margin, and every other sense is a version of it.
normal.cn: 看一页印刷纸：文字在中间，四周有一条白边。那条白边就是 margin，其他所有义项都是它的变体。

normal.en: A margin of error is a white strip around a measurement; buy on margin is a cash strip around a risky trade.
normal.cn: margin of error 是测量结果四周的白边；buy on margin 是一笔风险交易四周的现金缓冲。

normal.en: Profit margin is the strip between cost and price, thin or wide. It is a ratio, not the money itself.
normal.cn: profit margin 是成本与售价之间的那一条，可宽可窄。它是比率，不是钱本身。

normal.en: On the margins of society means at the edge of the page, outside the main text.
normal.cn: on the margins of society 就是处在纸页边缘、正文之外。

normal.en: The verb margin means writing in that strip: the place turns into an action.
normal.cn: 动词 margin 就是在那一条上写字：地点变成了动作。

abstract.en: Picture every important thing with a strip of empty space around it: a page, a score, a budget, a life. Margin is that strip, and its width tells you how safe or how thin things are.
abstract.cn: 想象每一件要紧的东西四周都留有一条空白：一页纸、一场比分、一份预算、一段人生。margin 就是那条空白，它的宽度告诉你事情有多安全、有多紧。

abstract.en: When the strip is inside a system it is tolerance; when it is inside a business it is profit; when it is inside a society it is exclusion.
abstract.cn: 当这条空白在系统内部，它是容差；在商业内部，它是利润；在社会内部，它是排斥。

abstract.en: The margin is never the centre, but nothing at the centre can be measured without it.
abstract.cn: 页边永远不是中心，但中心的一切都离不开它才能被量出来。

examples.en: The village sits at the margin of the forest and the marsh.
examples.cn: 这个村子位于森林与沼泽的边缘。

examples.en: The team won by a margin of two goals.
examples.cn: 这支球队以两球的差距获胜。

examples.en: Small shops survive on narrow margins and loyal customers.
examples.cn: 小店靠薄利和忠实顾客维持。

dict_mnemonic.text: “马诊”——马医生在页边空白处记下诊断，留出余地再下结论 → margin 页边、余地、差额

root: 拉丁语 margo（属格 marginis）“边缘、边界”，核心是“中心之外的那一条空间”，由页边引申为差额、余地、利润与保证金。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of margin, all one strip of reserved space: the edge of land, the blank page, a winning gap, a safety cushion, a profit ratio, broker's collateral, social periphery, a marginal note, and the boundary against edge and profit.
sensesIntro.cn: margin 的九个义项都是同一条被预留的空间：土地边缘、页边空白、胜负差距、安全余量、利润比率、经纪人保证金、社会边缘、页边批注，以及它与 edge、profit 的边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a strip of empty space runs between the centre and the outer limit.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条空白带介于中心与最外缘之间。

branches.en: LAND: the first sense is the physical rim where water, forest or field ends.
branches.cn: 土地：最早的义项是水域、森林或田野终止的实体外缘。

branches.en: PAGE: the blank strip around text, and the act of writing notes in it.
branches.cn: 纸页：文字四周的空白条，以及在其中写批注的动作。

branches.en: GAP: the measured space between two results is also the space kept free for safety.
branches.cn: 差距：两个结果之间被量出的空间，也是为安全而预留的空间。

branches.en: MONEY: cost and price leave a strip of profit; a broker holds a strip of collateral.
branches.cn: 金钱：成本与售价之间留下利润的那一条；经纪人手里握着保证金那一条。

branches.en: SOCIETY AND BOUNDARY: people at the edge of the page become marginal, and the strip is never a hard line.
branches.cn: 社会与边界：处在纸页边缘的人变成 marginal，而这条空白从不是一条硬线。

intro.en: Margin has no live English prefix. Its Latin stem margo, margin- is frozen inside; English adds -al, -ally, -alize and -alia to build the family.
intro.cn: margin 没有活的英语前缀。它的拉丁词干 margo、margin- 凝固在词内；英语加 -al、-ally、-alize、-alia 构成词族。

latinIntro.en: The *merg- 'boundary' root also underlies mark and march, which reached English through Germanic routes. Within English, the margin family is built on the Latin stem margin-.
latinIntro.cn: *merg-“边界”这个词根也支撑 mark 与 march，它们经日耳曼路径进入英语。在英语内部，margin 词族建立在拉丁词干 margin- 上。

items.meaning: written in a margin, situated at an edge, or small enough to be unimportant
items.meaningCN: 页边的；边缘的；微不足道的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The difference in cost is marginal.
items.exampleCN: 成本上的差别微不足道。

items.meaning: slightly, or at the edge
items.meaningCN: 略微；轻微地；在边缘地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The second design is marginally cheaper.
items.exampleCN: 第二个设计稍微便宜一点。

items.meaning: to push a person or group to the edge of influence
items.meaningCN: 使边缘化；把某人或群体排挤到影响力边缘（-ize 表示“使……化”）
items.example: Cheap transport marginalised the old market.
items.exampleCN: 廉价的交通让老市场边缘化了。

items.meaning: notes written in the margins of a book
items.meaningCN: 页边注；旁注（-ia 构成复数名词）
items.example: The library copy is full of marginalia.
items.exampleCN: 图书馆那本书上写满了旁注。

items.structure: Latin noun, third declension, genitive marginis
items.meaning: edge, border
items.example: The noun is the direct source of margin.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是 margin 的直接来源。

items.meaning: edge (combining form)
items.example: The stem appears in margin, marginal and marginalia.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干见于 margin、marginal 与 marginalia。

items.meaning: relating to
items.example: It forms marginal, belonging to the edge.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 marginal，即属于边缘的。

items.meaning: to make, to cause to be
items.example: It forms marginalize, to push to the edge.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 marginalize，即把……推向边缘。

items.meaning: a collection of things
items.example: It forms marginalia, notes written in the margins.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 marginalia，即写在页边的批注。

latinEntries.meaning: the act of marking a boundary
latinEntries.meaningCN: 划界；分界（标出边界）

latinEntries.meaning: a sign or boundary point
latinEntries.meaningCN: 标记；界标（原指边界记号）

latinEntries.meaning: borderland; the boundary region between two countries
latinEntries.meaningCN: 边境；边界地区

latinEntries.structure: Old French marchis (lord of a march) from marche (border)
latinEntries.meaning: a noble ranking below a duke, originally the lord of a border region
latinEntries.meaningCN: 侯爵（原指边境地区的领主）

definition_zh: 成熟的；成年的；深思熟虑的；使成熟；成熟；到期
definition_en: fully grown or fully developed, especially in fruit, wine, or a person; showing adult judgment; as a verb, to become fully developed or to reach the date when a financial product must be paid
core_image: 枝头的果子由青转红：酸涩退去，甜味与重量一起到位，才到了可以摘下的那一刻
scene: 果园里，农人捏了捏枝头的桃子。The peach gave slightly under his thumb, and only when it was mature did he cut it down and put it in the basket.
sceneCN: 这里 mature 是「果实成熟」（第 1 个义项：水果、作物达到可食用的成熟状态）；句意：桃子在他拇指下微微软了，只有确认它成熟了，他才摘下来放进筐里。图中可辨识物件：桃树枝、成熟的桃子、农人的手、果筐。

pos.zh: 成熟的；成年的；深思熟虑的；到期的
使成熟；成熟；到期

senses.title: Fruit or wine: ripe and ready
senses.titleCN: 果实或酒：熟到可以用了
senses.definition: of fruit, grain, or wine, fully ripened and ready to be eaten, harvested, or drunk
senses.definitionCN: 指水果、谷物或酒已完全成熟，可以食用、收割或饮用
senses.example: The peaches are mature enough to pick today.
senses.exampleCN: 这些桃子今天已经熟到可以摘了。
senses.why: The adjective is first recorded in the mid-15c. of fruits, meaning 'ripe, complete in natural growth or development'. The image is biological: growth has finished, and the fruit has reached the point it was growing toward.
senses.whyCN: 形容词义在 15 世纪中期首次记录，用于水果，意为“成熟的、在自然生长或发育上已完成的”。画面是生物性的：生长已经结束，果实到达了它一直生长所要到达的那一点。

senses.title: A person fully grown in body and mind
senses.titleCN: 身心发育完全的人
senses.definition: of a person, having fully developed powers of body and mind; adult
senses.definitionCN: 指人在身体与心智能力上已充分发育；成年的
senses.example: The study compares mature adults with teenagers.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究把成年人与青少年作比较。
senses.why: Of persons, the sense 'having fully developed powers of body and mind' is recorded c. 1600. The biological image is transferred from fruit to people: development has reached its intended end, though growth in learning may continue.
senses.whyCN: 用于人时，“身体与心智能力已充分发育”的义项记录于约 1600 年。生物意象从果实移到了人：发育已达到预定的终点，尽管学识上的成长仍可继续。

senses.title: Adult judgment: behaving with maturity
senses.titleCN: 成年人的判断力：表现得成熟
senses.definition: showing the emotional calm and responsibility expected of an adult, especially in a difficult situation
senses.definitionCN: 在困难处境中表现出成年人应有的情绪稳定与责任感
senses.example: She gave a mature answer instead of blaming someone else.
senses.exampleCN: 她没有责怪别人，而是给出了一个成熟的回答。
senses.why: This is the evaluative branch: mature no longer describes the body but the response. The word praises someone for having reached the emotional end-point that adulthood is supposed to bring.
senses.whyCN: 这是评价性的分支：mature 描述的不再是身体，而是反应方式。这个词在称赞一个人达到了成年本应带来的情绪终点。

senses.title: A well-considered plan or judgment
senses.titleCN: 经过充分考虑的计划或判断
senses.definition: of a plan, idea, or judgment, careful, thorough, and reached after long thought
senses.definitionCN: 指计划、想法或判断审慎、周全，并经过长时间思考才形成
senses.example: After months of review, they submitted a mature proposal.
senses.exampleCN: 经过数月审议，他们提交了一份成熟的方案。
senses.why: The same mid-15c. entry that named ripe fruit also named 'careful, well-considered, thorough' deliberations. An idea, like fruit, needs time before it is ready; rushing it gives a green, sour result.
senses.whyCN: 15 世纪中期记录“成熟果实”的同一条目，也记录了“审慎、周全、彻底”的思考。一个想法和果实一样，需要时间才能就绪；催熟只会得到青涩的结果。

senses.title: To ripen: make or become mature
senses.titleCN: 使成熟；变得成熟
senses.definition: to bring something to full ripeness, or to come to a state of ripeness
senses.definitionCN: 使某物完全成熟，或进入成熟状态
senses.example: The cheese is left to mature for eighteen months.
senses.exampleCN: 这种奶酪要放置十八个月让它成熟。
senses.why: The verb appears c. 1400 as 'encourage suppuration', then in the mid-15c. as 'cause to ripen'. The intransitive sense 'become ripe' is from the 1650s. The medical origin is literal: a swelling also comes to a head in its own time.
senses.whyCN: 动词义约在 1400 年出现，意为“促使化脓”，15 世纪中期转为“使成熟”。“自己变得成熟”的不及物义来自 17 世纪 50 年代。医学来源是字面的：肿胀也会在自己的时间里“长熟”。

senses.title: A market, product, or artist developing fully
senses.titleCN: 市场、产品或艺术家发展至完善
senses.definition: of an industry, product, style, or career, to develop over time into a settled and fully formed state
senses.definitionCN: 指行业、产品、风格或事业随时间发展，进入稳定而完整的状态
senses.example: The market matured quickly once the standards were agreed.
senses.exampleCN: 标准一旦达成一致，这个市场很快就成熟了。
senses.why: Growth in business follows the same curve as growth in a plant: an early unstable phase, then a settled phase. Calling a market mature means it has stopped expanding wildly and has found its shape.
senses.whyCN: 商业上的成长与植物的成长走同一条曲线：先是早期不稳定阶段，然后是稳定阶段。说一个市场 mature，意味着它已停止疯狂扩张，找到了自己的形状。

senses.title: Finance: reach the date of payment
senses.titleCN: 金融：到达付款日
senses.definition: of a bond, policy, or loan, to reach the date on which the principal must be paid
senses.definitionCN: 指债券、保单或贷款到达必须偿付本金的日期
senses.example: The bond matures in ten years, but the interest is paid twice a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这只债券十年后到期，但利息每年支付两次。
senses.why: The financial sense 'reach the time for payment' is recorded by 1861. A debt, like fruit, has a fixed season: it is not paid early, but at the point when it has become 'due', from Latin maturus 'timely'.
senses.whyCN: 金融义“到达付款时间”记录于 1861 年。债务和果实一样有固定的季节：不提前偿付，而是在它“到期”的那一点——maturus 本义就是“及时的”。

senses.title: A polite word for older
senses.titleCN: 对“年纪较大”的委婉说法
senses.definition: used as a polite or euphemistic adjective for someone older than the usual age for a role
senses.definitionCN: 用作礼貌或委婉的形容词，指比某角色的通常年龄更大
senses.example: She returned to university as a mature student at forty.
senses.exampleCN: 她四十岁时以成年学生的身份重返大学。
senses.why: The euphemistic sense 'older than usual' is recorded by 1953. Instead of saying old, English says mature, borrowing the positive idea of full development to avoid the negative idea of decline.
senses.whyCN: “比通常年龄更大”的委婉义记录于 1953 年。英语不说 old，而说 mature，借“充分发展”的正面含义，避开“衰退”的负面含义。

senses.title: Usage boundary: mature, ripe, adult, old
senses.titleCN: 用法边界：mature、ripe、adult、old
senses.definition: mature is broader than ripe and more evaluative than adult; it describes full development, not age itself, so it is not a neutral synonym of old
senses.definitionCN: mature 比 ripe 更宽，比 adult 更具评价性；它描述充分发展，而不是年龄本身，因此不是 old 的中性同义词
senses.example: A mature person may be young; a ripe fruit is simply ready to eat.
senses.exampleCN: 成熟的人可能很年轻；熟透的果子只是到了能吃的时候。
senses.why: Ripe belongs to fruit and grain; adult belongs to legal or biological age; mature adds judgment, readiness, and the completion of a process. The euphemistic use for age shows how easily the positive sense can be borrowed for a different purpose.
senses.whyCN: ripe 属于果实与谷物；adult 属于法定或生理年龄；mature 再加上判断力、就绪状态与过程的完成。用它对年龄作委婉表达，正说明这个正面义项多么容易被借去服务另一个目的。

intro.en: Mature comes from Latin maturus 'ripe, timely, early'. The word describes a process that has reached its proper point, and English extended it from fruit to people, plans, markets and debts. The deeper origin of maturus is not established.
intro.cn: mature 来自拉丁语 maturus“成熟的、及时的、早的”。这个词描述一个过程到达了它应有的节点，英语把它从果实扩展到人、计划、市场与债务。maturus 更深层的来源并未确立。

items.en: The verb is first recorded as maturen, 'encourage suppuration', then in the mid-15c. as 'cause to ripen, bring to maturity'. The earliest use is medical and agricultural, not moral.
items.cn: 动词最初记录为 maturen“促使化脓”，15 世纪中期转为“使成熟、带到成熟状态”。最早的用法是医学与农业的，而不是道德评价的。

items.en: The adjective appears of fruits, 'ripe, complete in natural growth or development', and of deliberations, 'careful, well-considered, thorough'.
items.cn: 形容词义出现，用于水果时意为“成熟的、自然生长或发育已完成的”，用于思考时意为“审慎的、周全的、彻底的”。

items.en: From Latin maturus 'ripe, timely, early', also the source of maturare 'to ripen, bring to maturity'. The link with mane 'early, of the morning' is standard.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 maturus“成熟的、及时的、早的”，也是 maturare“使成熟、带到成熟状态”的来源。它与 mane“早、清晨”的联系是通行说法。

items.en: The deeper origin of maturus is source uncertain. Some references cautiously connect it with a notion of 'ripeness' or with Latin manus 'good'; these are proposals, not established derivations, so no confident PIE root should be asserted.
items.cn: maturus 更深层的来源不确定。一些资料谨慎地把它与“成熟”的观念或拉丁语 manus“好”相联系；这些只是推测，不是已确立的派生关系，因此不应断言某个确定的原始印欧语词根。

items.en: Of persons, 'having fully developed powers of body and mind' is recorded c. 1600. The intransitive sense 'become ripe' follows in the 1650s.
items.cn: 用于人时，“身体与心智能力已充分发育”记录于约 1600 年。不及物义“变得成熟”随后在 17 世纪 50 年代出现。

items.en: The financial sense 'reach the time for payment' is recorded by 1861; the euphemistic sense 'older than usual' by 1953.
items.cn: 金融义“到达付款时间”记录于 1861 年；“比通常年龄更大”的委婉义记录于 1953 年。

note.en: The first group shares the maturus stem and its prefixes. The second group separates ripeness, legal adulthood, everyday grown-up behaviour and the softening that comes with age.
note.cn: 第一组共享 maturus 词干及其前缀。第二组区分果实成熟、法定成年、日常的“大人样”，以及随年龄而来的柔和。

entries.definition: the state of being mature, or the date when a financial product must be paid. It is the noun from mature.
entries.definitionCN: 成熟状态，或金融产品的到期日。它是 mature 的名词。

entries.definition: not fully developed, or behaving below the expected adult level. It adds the negative prefix in- to maturus.
entries.definitionCN: 未充分发育的，或行为低于成年人应有水平的。它在 maturus 前加了否定前缀 in-。

entries.definition: happening before the proper or expected time, as in a premature birth or a premature conclusion.
entries.definitionCN: 在应有或预期时间之前发生的，如早产或过早的结论。

entries.definition: ready to be eaten or harvested, especially of fruit or grain. It is narrower and more physical than mature.
entries.definitionCN: 可以食用或收割的，尤指水果或谷物。它比 mature 更窄、更具体。

entries.definition: fully grown or legally of age. It marks a stage of life, while mature also judges behaviour and judgment.
entries.definitionCN: 发育完全或达到法定年龄。它标记人生阶段，而 mature 还评价行为与判断力。

entries.definition: adult, or behaving in an adult way. It is more conversational and less evaluative than mature.
entries.definitionCN: 成年的，或表现得像大人。它比 mature 更口语化，评价性更弱。

entries.definition: softened and pleasant with age, as of wine, sound, or a person. It stresses gentleness, while mature stresses completion.
entries.definitionCN: 随年龄变得柔和、悦人，如酒、声音或人。它强调温和，而 mature 强调完成。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: maturus 'ripe, timely' gives mature, maturity, maturation, premature and immature; mane 'early' gives matins and matutinal.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词与真实同族词：maturus“成熟的、及时的”给出 mature、maturity、maturation、premature、immature；mane“早”给出 matins、matutinal。

normal.en: Mature is a process word: something has reached the point it was growing toward. Fruit, wine, a person, a plan, a market and a bond can all arrive there.
normal.cn: mature 是一个过程词：某物到达了它一直生长所要到达的那一点。果实、酒、人、计划、市场、债券都可以到达那里。

normal.en: maturus means 'ripe' and also 'timely'. A mature bond is not old; it has simply reached its proper time.
normal.cn: maturus 既指“成熟”，也指“及时”。到期的债券不是“老”，它只是到达了它该到的时间。

normal.en: The verb first meant 'encourage suppuration' c. 1400: even an abscess was thought to come to a head in its own time. Ripening is a natural clock, not a push.
normal.cn: 动词约在 1400 年最早表示“促使化脓”：连脓肿也被认为会在自己的时间里“长熟”。成熟是一只自然的钟，不是硬推。

normal.en: The euphemism mature student (1953) borrows the positive sense of full development to avoid the word old.
normal.cn: mature student（1953）这个委婉说法，借“充分发展”的正面含义来避开 old 这个词。

normal.en: immature and premature are mature with a negative or a 'before' prefix: not yet developed, or developed too soon.
normal.cn: immature 与 premature 是给 mature 加上否定或“之前”的前缀：尚未发展，或发展得太早。

abstract.en: Picture a clock with no hands: you cannot see the time, only whether the fruit is still hard or finally soft. Mature is the moment the process says 'now'.
abstract.cn: 想象一只没有指针的钟：你看不见时间，只能看见果子还是硬的、或终于软了。mature 就是过程说出“现在”的那一刻。

abstract.en: The same curve runs through a peach, a wine, a mind, a manuscript, an industry and a debt: slow completion, then readiness.
abstract.cn: 同一条曲线穿过桃子、酒、心智、手稿、产业与债务：缓慢完成，然后就绪。

abstract.en: What is mature is not old; it is finished enough to be used. Old age is only one of the places where that readiness can be seen.
abstract.cn: 成熟的东西不是“老”，而是“完成到可以使用”。年老只是这种就绪状态可能被看见的场所之一。

examples.en: The wine needs another five years to mature properly.
examples.cn: 这酒还需要再放五年才能好好成熟。

examples.en: He handled the criticism in a mature way.
examples.cn: 他以成熟的方式对待批评。

examples.en: The loan matures at the end of March.
examples.cn: 这笔贷款在三月底到期。

dict_mnemonic.text: “马球”——马球运动员等到果子熟了才开赛，说这是成熟的决定 → mature 成熟的

root: 拉丁语 maturus“成熟的、及时的”，核心是“过程走到应有的节点、可以用了”，更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of mature, one ripening curve: ripe fruit, a grown person, adult judgment, a considered plan, the act of ripening, a settled market, a due debt, a polite word for older, and the boundary against ripe and old.
sensesIntro.cn: mature 的九个义项都是同一条成熟曲线：熟果、发育完全的人、成年人的判断、深思熟虑的计划、成熟的动作、稳定的市场、到期的债务、对年长的委婉说法，以及它与 ripe、old 的边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a process reaches its proper point, and what has grown is now ready.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个过程到达了应有的节点，长成的东西现在可以用了。

branches.en: FRUIT AND WINE: biological ripening is the literal source of the whole family.
branches.cn: 果实与酒：生物性的成熟是整个词族最字面的来源。

branches.en: PERSON: the body finishes growing, and behaviour is expected to finish growing too.
branches.cn: 人：身体完成生长，行为也被期待完成“长大”。

branches.en: PROCESS: a plan and a market both need time before they are ready to be used.
branches.cn: 过程：计划与市场都需要时间，才能就绪可用。

branches.en: FINANCE: a debt has a season, and maturing is reaching that date.
branches.cn: 金融：债务有它的季节，到期就是走到那个日期。

branches.en: EUPHEMISM AND BOUNDARY: age is softened by the positive sense, and mature never simply means old.
branches.cn: 委婉与边界：年龄被正面义项柔化，而 mature 从不简单等于 old。

intro.en: Mature takes Latin prefixes and English suffixes: im- and pre- negate or shift time, while -ity, -ly and -ation build nouns and adverbs. The stem matur- stays constant.
intro.cn: mature 接受拉丁前缀与英语后缀：im- 与 pre- 表示否定或时间偏移，-ity、-ly、-ation 构成名词与副词。词干 matur- 保持不变。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family joins maturus 'ripe, timely' with mane 'early, morning': matins and matutinal belong to the morning, while premature means ripening before its time.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族把 maturus“成熟的、及时的”与 mane“早、清晨”连在一起：matins 与 matutinal 属于清晨，premature 则指在时间之前就成熟。

items.meaning: the state of being fully developed; the date a financial product is due
items.meaningCN: 成熟；成熟期；到期（-ity 构成状态名词）
items.example: The bond reaches maturity next year.
items.exampleCN: 这只债券明年到期。

items.meaning: in a mature, calm, and considered way
items.meaningCN: 成熟地；深思熟虑地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: She responded maturely to the criticism.
items.exampleCN: 她对批评作出了成熟的回应。

items.meaning: not fully developed, or not behaving at an adult level
items.meaningCN: 未成熟的；幼稚的（im- 表示否定）
items.example: The fruit is still immature and should be left on the tree.
items.exampleCN: 果子还没成熟，应该留在树上。

items.meaning: happening before the proper time
items.meaningCN: 过早的；早产的（pre- 表示“在……之前”）
items.example: It is premature to announce a result.
items.exampleCN: 现在宣布结果还为时过早。

items.meaning: ripe, timely, fully developed
items.example: The adjective is the direct source of mature.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是 mature 的直接来源。

items.meaning: ripe (combining form)
items.example: The stem appears in mature, maturity and maturation.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干见于 mature、maturity 与 maturation。

items.meaning: quality or state
items.example: It forms maturity, the state of being ripe.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 maturity，即成熟状态。

items.meaning: a process or its result
items.example: It forms maturation, the process of ripening.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 maturation，即成熟过程。

items.meaning: the state of not being mature
items.example: The review criticized the immaturity of the plan.
items.exampleCN: 评审批评了这份计划的不成熟。

latinEntries.structure: Latin matutinus (of the morning) from mane (early)
latinEntries.meaning: a morning church service
latinEntries.meaningCN: 晨祷（清晨的礼拜）

latinEntries.meaning: relating to the morning; early
latinEntries.meaningCN: 清晨的；早起的

latinEntries.meaning: the quality of happening or developing before the proper time
latinEntries.meaningCN: 过早；早产（在应有时间之前发生或发育的状态）

latinEntries.meaning: the process of becoming mature
latinEntries.meaningCN: 成熟过程；成熟化
